definition_en: relating to sound that is recorded or broadcast, or the recorded sound itself
core_image: 一排跳动的波形，把看不见的声音画成看得见的线
scene: 剪辑师把画面定住，先单独处理声音那条轨道。The audio was clearer than the video.
sceneCN: 这里 audio 是「音频、声音信号」（第 2 个义项）；句意是音频比画面清楚。

pos.zh: 形容词：声音的；音频的
名词：音频；声音信号

forms.label: 不可数名词与形容词（无屈折变化）

senses.title: Relating to sound
senses.definition: connected with sound that is recorded, played back or broadcast
senses.definitionCN: 与录制、播放或播出的声音有关的
senses.example: The audio cable was loose at the back.
senses.exampleCN: 音频线在后面松了。
senses.why: As an adjective it simply labels the sound side of any system, standing opposite video in the same sentence.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，它只是给任何系统里「声音那一侧」贴标签，在同一句里与 video 相对。

senses.title: The sound itself
senses.definition: the recorded or transmitted sound itself
senses.definitionCN: 被录制或传输的声音本身
senses.example: The audio was clearer than the video.
senses.exampleCN: 音频比画面清楚。
senses.why: As a noun it turns the adjective into a mass of data: not a sound in the air, but a signal stored in a file.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，形容词变成了可供处理的一团数据：不是空气里的声音，而是存在文件里的信号。

senses.title: The sound channel in a mix
senses.definition: the sound track of a recording or film, handled separately from the picture
senses.definitionCN: 录音或影片中与画面分开处理的那条声音通道
senses.example: Turn down the audio and leave the picture as it is.
senses.exampleCN: 把声音调小，画面保持原样。
senses.why: In editing, sound is a lane that can be moved, cut or muted on its own, so the word also names that lane.
senses.whyCN: 剪辑时声音是一条可以单独移动、剪切或静音的轨道，于是这个词也指那条轨道本身。

senses.title: Sound equipment as a trade label
senses.definition: the equipment that records or plays sound, used as a short label in shops and studios
senses.definitionCN: 录制或播放声音的设备，在商店与录音棚里用作简称
senses.example: The shop sells audio and cameras on the same floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这家商店在同一层卖音响和相机。
senses.why: Trade language shortens a whole department to one word, so the label can stand for the goods rather than the signal.
senses.whyCN: 行业用语习惯把整个部门缩成一个词，于是这个标签也能指那一类商品，而不只是信号。

senses.title: The scientific element for hearing
senses.definition: the element used in technical words for hearing and for measuring it
senses.definitionCN: 技术词汇中表示「听、听觉」并用于测量听觉的构词成分
senses.example: Audio- opens audiometer, the instrument that tests how faint a sound a person can hear.
senses.exampleCN: 「听」这个成分出现在听力计一词的开头，那是一种测人能听到多弱声音的仪器。
senses.why: Science kept the Latin stem alive as a prefix, so the same element that names a file also names the study of the ear.
senses.whyCN: 科学界把拉丁词干保留为前缀，于是同一个成分既能命名文件，也能命名对耳朵的研究。

intro.en: Audio is simply the Latin word for 'I hear', taken whole into modern technology.
intro.cn: audio 就是拉丁语「我听见」，被整体搬进了现代技术。

items.en: Latin audire meant to hear, and its participle stem audit- built the whole family of hearing words.
items.cn: 拉丁语 audire 意为「听」，其分词词干 audit- 撑起了整个「听」词族。

items.en: Audio was the first person singular of that verb, literally I hear, and it survived as a label rather than a sentence.
items.cn: audio 是这个动词的第一人称单数形式，字面意思是「我听见」，后来作为标签而非句子留存下来。

items.en: Nineteenth-century science used audi- for instruments and for the study of hearing, as in audiometer and audiology.
items.cn: 十九世纪科学界用 audi- 命名仪器与听觉研究，例如听力计与听觉学。

items.en: With radio and film, audio became the standard name for the sound channel, paired with video for the picture.
items.cn: 随着广播与电影出现，audio 成为声音通道的标准名称，与表示画面的视频一词配对。

items.en: Tape and then digital files turned the word into a mass noun: an audio file holds sound as data.
items.cn: 磁带与随后的数字文件把这个词变成不可数名词：音频文件把声音当作数据存放。

items.en: Today audio covers streams, cables, equipment and settings, and it is the everyday opposite of video.
items.cn: 如今 audio 涵盖流媒体、线材、设备与设置，是日常语中与视频相对的那一半。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the aud- root; the near-meaning group gives other words for sound.
note.cn: 形近组共享 aud- 词根；近义组是其他表示声音的词。

definition_zh: 审计；查账；审查，核查；税务稽查；（大学）旁听
definition_en: an official examination of accounts or of how something is done, or the act of making such an examination; in American universities, to attend a class without taking it for credit
core_image: 账本摊开，一笔笔念出来，旁边有人听着核对
scene: 年终结算前，会计把一摞凭证摊在长桌上，等外人来逐笔核对。The firm hired an outside team to audit its accounts.
sceneCN: 这里 audit 是动词「审计、查账」（第 4 个义项）；句意是公司请外部团队来审计账目。

pos.zh: 名词：审计；审查；稽查
及物动词：审计；核查；旁听

derivatives.zh: 同根加指人词尾：审计师；旁听生
动名词固化：审计工作；审计学
加否定前缀：未经审计的

senses.title: An official check of accounts
senses.definition: an official examination of the financial records of a company or person to confirm that they are accurate
senses.definitionCN: 对公司或个人的财务记录进行正式检查，以确认其准确无误
senses.example: The annual audit found two payments without receipts.
senses.exampleCN: 年度审计发现两笔付款没有收据。
senses.why: Accounts were once read aloud while an official listened and checked, so the noun still names a hearing of the books.
senses.whyCN: 从前账目要大声念出来，由官员听着核对，所以这个名词至今仍是「听账」的意思。

senses.title: A systematic review of practice
senses.definition: a structured examination of how a process, service or site meets a stated standard
senses.definitionCN: 对某个流程、服务或场所是否符合既定标准所作的系统性检查
senses.example: A safety audit closed the workshop for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一次安全审查让车间停工了一周。
senses.why: The idea of an independent person checking against a rule transfers from money to any measurable practice.
senses.whyCN: 「由独立的人对照规则来核对」这一想法从钱款推广到任何可衡量的做法。

senses.title: A tax examination
senses.definition: an official check by the tax office of what a person or firm has declared
senses.definitionCN: 税务机关对申报内容进行的正式核查
senses.example: He kept every invoice in case of a tax audit.
senses.exampleCN: 他把每张发票都留着，以防税务稽查。
senses.why: The state is the listener who must be satisfied, so the same word names its inspection of your figures.
senses.whyCN: 国家就是那个必须被说服的「听者」，于是同一个词也指它对你数字的检查。

senses.title: To examine accounts officially
senses.definition: to examine financial records officially and report whether they are correct
senses.definitionCN: 正式检查财务记录并报告其是否正确
senses.example: An outside firm was asked to audit the accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 一家外部事务所受邀审计这些账目。
senses.why: The noun became a verb without changing form, keeping the picture of an outsider going through the books line by line.
senses.whyCN: 名词不经变形直接用作动词，保留了「外人逐行翻账」的画面。

senses.title: To review how something is done
senses.definition: to check a process, stock or performance against a standard and record the result
senses.definitionCN: 对照标准检查流程、库存或表现，并记录结果
senses.example: The team audited its own energy use.
senses.exampleCN: 团队核查了自己的能耗。
senses.why: Once the object need not be money, the verb simply means a disciplined check supported by evidence.
senses.whyCN: 一旦对象不必是钱款，这个动词就泛指有凭有据、按规矩做的检查。

senses.title: To attend a class without credit
senses.definition: to attend a university course without taking examinations or earning credit
senses.definitionCN: 在大学里听课但不参加考试、不取学分
senses.example: She audited a course in medieval history.
senses.exampleCN: 她旁听了一门中世纪史课程。
senses.why: American colleges kept the old sense of a listener present at a hearing: the student hears but is not examined.
senses.whyCN: 美国高校保留了「在场听审」的旧义：学生只是听，而不接受考核。

senses.title: A private stocktaking
senses.definition: a careful review of one's own habits, time or possessions
senses.definitionCN: 对自己的习惯、时间或物品所作的仔细清点
senses.example: A weekend audit of her subscriptions saved a lot of money.
senses.exampleCN: 周末对自己订阅服务的一次盘点省下了不少钱。
senses.why: The professional word lends its seriousness to private life, so any honest count of what is really there can be called an audit.
senses.whyCN: 专业词把它的严肃劲儿借给了私人生活，于是任何如实清点都可以叫这个名字。

intro.en: Audit belongs to the Latin hearing family: accounts were read aloud and an official listened, so checking the books is literally a hearing.
intro.cn: audit 属于拉丁语「听」词族：账目被大声宣读，由官员听着核对，所以查账在字面上就是一场「听审」。

items.en: The hearing family is generally traced to a root meaning to perceive, which combined with another element to give Latin audire; the reconstructed shape is debated.
items.cn: 「听」词族一般被认为出自表示「感知」的词根，与另一成分复合后产生拉丁语 audire；具体重构形式有争议。

items.en: Audire meant to hear, and its participle stem audit- supplied the nouns and adjectives of the family.
items.cn: audire 意为「听」，其分词词干 audit- 提供了这个词族的名词与形容词。

items.en: Auditus named a hearing or listening, and in administration it came to mean the hearing of accounts.
items.cn: auditus 指「听、倾听」这一行为，在行政语境中引申为「听取账目」。

items.en: Accounts were read aloud before an official who listened and questioned the steward, because many people present could not read.
items.cn: 账目要在官员面前大声宣读，由他听着并向管家质询，因为在场许多人并不识字。

items.en: English took the word in the fifteenth century for an official examination of accounts, and later used it as a verb.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个词，指对账目的正式检查，后来又用作动词。

items.en: The noun spread to safety, quality and energy checks, while American colleges kept the verb for sitting in a class without credit.
items.cn: 这个名词扩展到安全、质量与能耗检查，而美国高校则保留「旁听」这一动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the Latin hearing family, with one false friend; the near-meaning group grades kinds of checking.
note.cn: 形近组留在拉丁语「听」词族内部，并掺入一个假朋友；近义组按检查的种类分级。

entries.definition: the act of confirming that something is true

normalIntro.en: Audit is a hearing of the books: someone reads, someone listens, and the numbers must answer.
normalIntro.cn: audit 是一场「听账」：有人念，有人听，数字必须对得上。

normal.en: The stem audit- comes from the Latin verb for hear.
normal.cn: 词干 audit- 出自拉丁语表示「听」的动词。

normal.en: An audit ends in a report, not just a look.

normal.en: To audit a class is to hear it without credit.

normal.en: Audacious only looks similar; it comes from a root for daring.
normal.cn: audacious 只是形近，它出自「敢」的词根。

abstract.en: Picture two columns, one read and one ticked.

abstract.en: Picture a student at the back who never sits an exam.
abstract.cn: 想象一个坐在后排、从不参加考试的学生。

examples.en: The audit revealed a gap in the petty cash.
examples.cn: 审计发现零用现金有一处缺口。

examples.en: An outside firm will audit the accounts this spring.
examples.cn: 今年春天将由一家外部事务所审计账目。

examples.en: She audited two lectures a week and took no exams.
examples.cn: 她每周旁听两节课，不参加考试。

sensesIntro.en: From a hearing of accounts the word spreads to any evidenced check, then turns into a verb, and finally names the listener who sits in a class.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「听账」出发，这个词扩展到任何有凭有据的检查，再转为动词，最后落到坐在教室里只听不考的人。

senses.title: A test performance for a role
senses.definition: a short trial performance to judge a performer's suitability for a part
senses.definitionCN: 为判断表演者是否胜任某角色而进行的简短测试表演
senses.example: She got the lead role after a single audition.
senses.exampleCN: 仅一次试演后她就拿到了主角。
senses.why: The root is hearing: the judges decide with their ears, so the trial is named after listening.
senses.whyCN: 词根是「听」：考官用耳朵裁决，这场测试便以「听」命名。

senses.title: To take part in such a test
senses.definition: to perform at an audition in the hope of being chosen
senses.definitionCN: 参加试演，以求被选中
senses.example: Three hundred dancers auditioned for the show.
senses.exampleCN: 三百名舞者为这档节目参加了试演。
senses.why: The noun slid into a verb without effort, as English names do.
senses.whyCN: 名词毫不费力地转为动词，这是英语命名的一贯做法。

senses.title: To test someone by a trial performance
senses.definition: to ask a performer to give a trial performance in order to judge them
senses.definitionCN: 请表演者进行测试表演以便评估
senses.example: The director auditioned over a hundred children for the film.
senses.exampleCN: 导演为这部电影试演了一百多名孩子。
senses.why: The verb faces both ways: the performer auditions, and the director auditions them.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可双向使用：表演者参加试演，导演也「试演」表演者。

senses.title: The sense of hearing
senses.definition: the sense or power of hearing, especially in scientific use
senses.definitionCN: 听觉能力，多用于科学语境
senses.example: Bats rely on audition to navigate in the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 蝙蝠依靠听觉在黑暗中导航。
senses.why: The Latin audire gives hearing a formal noun; science revived this older sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 audire 为听觉提供了正式名词；科学界重新启用了这一旧义。

senses.title: A trial of anything by listening
senses.definition: a trial of a musician, instrument, or recording by listening to it
senses.definitionCN: 通过试听来检验乐手、乐器或录音
senses.example: The orchestra held auditions for a new first violin.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团为新任首席小提琴举办试奏。
senses.why: Musicians audition with sound alone, so the listening root fits them most literally.
senses.whyCN: 乐手单凭声音应试，「听」的词根在他们身上最为贴切。

senses.title: A formal hearing or interview
senses.definition: in older use, a formal interview or opportunity to be heard by someone important
senses.definitionCN: 旧义：正式接见，或在要人面前陈情的机会
senses.example: The ambassador was granted an audition with the queen.
senses.exampleCN: 大使获女王正式接见。
senses.why: Before casting calls, an audition meant simply a hearing before power.
senses.whyCN: 在试镜出现之前，audition 就是「在权贵面前得闻」之意。

senses.title: A tryout in extended use
senses.definition: any test that decides whether someone or something qualifies
senses.definitionCN: 决定某人或某物是否合格的任何考验
senses.example: Every crisis is an audition for leadership.
senses.exampleCN: 每场危机都是对领导力的检验。
senses.why: The judged-performance idea spread from stage to life, where leaders too perform for judges.
senses.whyCN: 「被审视的表演」这一概念从舞台延伸到人生——领导者同样要在评审面前表演。

senses.title: In audiology and animal studies
senses.definition: hearing as studied in audiology and animal behavior
senses.definitionCN: 听力科学与动物行为学所研究的听觉
senses.example: The study measured audition in older adults.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究测量了老年人的听觉。
senses.why: Technical writing prefers audition when it wants a precise, neutral noun for hearing.
senses.whyCN: 当技术文献需要一个精确中立的听觉名词时，便会选用 audition。

intro.en: Audition comes from Latin auditio, a hearing, formed on audire, to hear; English first used it for the sense of hearing and for a formal hearing, and only in the late nineteenth century for a test performance.
intro.cn: audition 出自拉丁语 auditio「听」，基础为动词 audire「听」；英语最初用它指听觉与正式接见，19 世纪末才转指测试表演。

items.en: The root *h₂ewis- meant to perceive, to hear, the shared source of the Latin hearing family.
items.cn: 词根 *h₂ewis- 意为「感知、听见」，是拉丁语「听」词族的共同源头。

items.en: audire meant to hear; its participle stem audit- supplied auditio, a hearing or listening.
items.cn: 拉丁语 audire 意为「听」；其分词词干 audit- 构成 auditio，意为「听；倾听」。

items.en: auditio named both the act of hearing and, in rhetoric, a case argued before a judge.
items.cn: auditio 既指「听」这一行为，在修辞学中也指在裁判前申辩的案件。

items.en: audition entered English meaning the sense of hearing and, by extension, a formal hearing before a great person.
items.cn: audition 进入英语时指听觉，引申为在显贵面前的正式接见。

items.en: The theatrical sense arose in the late nineteenth century: a trial performance is a hearing for the ears of the judges.
items.cn: 戏剧义产生于 19 世纪末：测试表演就是一场呈于考官耳中的「听审」。

items.en: Today the theatrical verb and noun dominate, while science keeps the older hearing sense in audition and audiology.
items.cn: 如今戏剧义的动名词占主导，而科学界仍在 audition 与 audiology 中保留古老的听觉义。

note.en: Group one collects the hearing family and aud- look-alikes; group two collects neighboring tryout and hearing words.
note.cn: 第一组收「听」词族及 aud- 形近词；第二组收相邻的「测试」与「听觉」词。

entries.definition: the listeners themselves, from Latin audientia.
entries.definitionCN: 听众；观众，出自拉丁语 audientia。

entries.definition: relating to hearing; the adjective sibling of audition's hearing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 听觉的；audition 听觉义的形容词同胞词。

entries.definition: one who audits accounts; historically, a listener. Related root, different line.
entries.definitionCN: 审计员；历史上指「听者」。同根异流。

entries.definition: bold, from audare, to dare; shares only the aud- spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的，出自「敢」的词根；仅拼写同以 aud- 开头。

entries.definition: a printed version, from Latin editio, a giving out; one letter apart, unrelated root.
entries.definitionCN: 版本，出自拉丁语 editio「刊行」；仅差一个字母，词根无关。

entries.definition: an informal audition or trial, common in sports.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式的试演或选拔，体育中常用。

entries.definition: a formal meeting to judge suitability, for jobs rather than roles.
entries.definitionCN: 面试；用于求职而非选角。

entries.definition: a public announcement inviting people to audition.
entries.definitionCN: 选角公告；邀请人们来试镜。

entries.definition: the everyday word for the sense that audition names formally.
entries.definitionCN: 听觉的日常说法；audition 是其正式对应。

entries.definition: a filmed audition for film or television.
entries.definitionCN: 为影视拍摄的试镜录像。

normalIntro.en: audition is a hearing: audi for listen, -tion for the act, first of ears, then of judges.
normalIntro.cn: audition 就是一场「听审」：audi 表「听」，-tion 表行为——先属于耳朵，后属于考官。

normal.en: audi + tion: the act of hearing, exactly like edition is the act of giving out.
normal.cn: audi + tion：听的行为，正如 edition 是刊行的行为。

normal.en: An audition is literally a hearing before the people who decide.
normal.cn: 试演的字面义就是在裁决者面前「受审听」。

normal.en: The family: audible, audience, auditorium, audition, auditory.
normal.cn: 同族词：audible、audience、auditorium、audition、auditory。

normal.en: audition for a role is the set verb pattern to memorize.
normal.cn: audition for a role 是值得记牢的动词搭配。

normal.en: In science, audition just means hearing, no stage required.
normal.cn: 在科学语境里，audition 就指听觉，与舞台无关。

abstract.en: Picture one chair, one spotlight, and three silent ears behind a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子、一束追光，和桌后三只沉默的耳朵。

abstract.en: The word holds its breath before the first note.
abstract.cn: 这个词在第一个音符前屏住呼吸。

abstract.en: Audition is a door that opens only for a performed minute.
abstract.cn: audition 是一扇只为一段表演敞开一分钟的门。

examples.en: He practiced the monologue for weeks before the audition.
examples.cn: 试演前他花了数周练习那段独白。

examples.en: Over a thousand singers auditioned for the talent show.
examples.cn: 上千名歌手报名参加了选秀节目的试音。

examples.en: Age slowly dulls the sense of audition.
examples.cn: 听觉会随年龄增长而逐渐迟钝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥迪逊」——开着奥迪去参加比赛，第一个上场试音

root: 出自拉丁语 auditio「听；倾听」（动词 audire「听」的分词词干 audit- + 抽象名词后缀 -io），16 世纪进入英语时指听觉与正式接见，19 世纪末引申为「测试表演」；与 audience、audio、audible 同属「听」词族，词源确凿。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one noun from ears to stage: hearing itself, a formal hearing, and the judged performance the theater made of it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项追溯一个名词从耳朵走向舞台的轨迹：听觉本身、正式接见，以及戏剧界由此造出的测试表演。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a performed minute laid before judging ears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段表演被呈递到裁决的耳朵面前。

branches.en: THE STAGE SIDE: trial performances for actors and musicians.
branches.cn: 舞台一面：演员与乐手的测试表演。

branches.en: THE VERB SIDE: to audition and to audition someone.
branches.cn: 动词一面：参加试演与试演某人。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE SIDE: hearing as a measured sense.
branches.cn: 科学一面：作为可测官能的听觉。

branches.en: THE OLD SIDE: a formal hearing before power.
branches.cn: 旧义一面：在权势面前的正式接见。

branches.en: THE EXTENDED SIDE: life's crises as auditions for character.
branches.cn: 引申一面：人生的危机成为品格的试演。

intro.en: audition is the stem audit- plus -ion, the Latin way to name an act; the same stem powers auditory and auditor.
intro.cn: audition 由词干 audit- 加 -ion 构成，这是拉丁语为「行为」命名的方式；同一词干也支撑着 auditory 与 auditor。

latinIntro.en: Latin audire, to hear, anchors the family: audible, audience, audio, auditory, auditorium, audition.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 audire「听」统率词族：audible、audience、audio、auditory、auditorium、audition。

items.meaning: a listener; later, one who examines accounts

definition_zh: 审计师；查账员；稽核员；（大学）旁听生；（古义）听者
definition_en: a person whose job is to examine accounts or to check that rules are followed; in American universities, a student who attends a class without credit; formerly, a listener
core_image: 外人坐在长桌对面，逐笔听账、逐笔打钩
scene: 事务所派来的人翻开凭证，一笔一笔问到深夜。The auditor asked for every receipt from the last quarter.
sceneCN: 这里 auditor 是「审计师、查账员」（第 1 个义项）；句意是审计师索要上一季度的每一张收据。

pos.zh: 名词：审计师；稽核员；旁听生；听者

derivatives.zh: 加「职位」后缀：审计师的职位

senses.title: A professional examiner of accounts
senses.definition: a qualified person whose job is to examine financial records and report on them
senses.definitionCN: 以检查财务记录并出具报告为职业的专业人员
senses.example: The auditor signed the report without qualification.
senses.exampleCN: 审计师无保留地签署了报告。
senses.why: Latin auditor meant a hearer, and accounts were once read aloud to him, so the job title still carries the ear.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语里这个词意为「听的人」，账目从前是念给他听的，所以这个职称至今仍带着耳朵。

senses.title: An inspector of rules and systems
senses.definition: a person who checks that an organization follows rules, standards or its own procedures
senses.definitionCN: 检查某机构是否遵守规则、标准或自身流程的人
senses.example: A quality auditor visited the plant twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 质量稽核员每年到厂两次。
senses.why: The listening role generalized: what is checked need not be money, only something that must match a rule.
senses.whyCN: 「听审」的角色被推广：被检查的不必是钱款，只要是必须与规则相符的东西即可。

senses.title: A student listening without credit
senses.definition: a student who attends a university course without taking examinations or earning credit
senses.definitionCN: 在大学听课但不参加考试、不取学分的学生
senses.example: The professor welcomed auditors to the back rows.
senses.exampleCN: 教授欢迎旁听生坐到后排。
senses.why: American usage returned to the literal Latin sense: a person who hears, and nothing more.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法回到了拉丁语的字面义：一个听的人，仅此而已。

senses.title: A hearer in older English
senses.definition: in older English, a person who listens to a speaker or to a reading
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的英语里，指听人讲话或听朗读的人
senses.example: The old sermon warned the auditor to remember what he heard.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇旧布道文告诫听者要记住所听的内容。
senses.why: This is the untouched Latin meaning, kept in writing long after the accounting sense took over.
senses.whyCN: 这是未经引申的拉丁语本义，在「查账」义占主导之后仍留在书面语中。

senses.title: The audit firm as one body
senses.definition: the firm or office that carries out an audit, referred to as a single actor
senses.definitionCN: 执行审计的事务所或部门，被当作一个行为主体来指称
senses.example: The auditor must be independent of the company.
senses.exampleCN: 审计方必须独立于被审计公司。
senses.why: Institutional language lets one noun stand for a whole team, so the word can mean the firm rather than one person.
senses.whyCN: 机构性语言允许一个名词代表整个团队，于是这个词可以指事务所而不是某一个人。

intro.en: Auditor is the agent noun of the Latin hearing family: the one who hears, first in a hall, later over a ledger.
intro.cn: auditor 是拉丁语「听」词族的施动者名词：听的那个人，先在厅堂里听，后来在账本上听。

items.en: The Latin verb for hear is generally linked to a root meaning to perceive; the reconstructed compound is disputed in detail.
items.cn: 拉丁语表示「听」的动词一般被认为与「感知」词根有关；重构的复合形式在细节上有争议。

items.en: Audire meant to hear, and its participle stem audit- was the base for agent nouns.
items.cn: audire 意为「听」，其分词词干 audit- 是指人名词的构词基础。

items.en: Auditor meant a hearer or listener, and in Roman administration an official who heard accounts and claims.
items.cn: auditor 意为「听者」，在罗马行政中也指听取账目与申诉的官员。

items.en: Medieval courts and monasteries appointed auditors to hear accounts read aloud and to question the steward.
items.cn: 中世纪的宫廷与修道院指派专人听账，并向管家提出质询。

items.en: English took the word in the late fourteenth century for an examiner of accounts.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪晚期借入这个词，指查账的人。

items.en: Nineteenth-century American colleges used the word for a student who only listens, reviving the plain Latin sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪美国高校用这个词指只听课的学生，复活了拉丁语的朴素本义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the hearing family with one false friend; the near-meaning group separates financial jobs by what they actually do.
note.cn: 形近组是「听」词族加一个假朋友；近义组按实际工作内容区分各种财务岗位。

entries.definition: the examination itself
entries.definitionCN: 审计这件事；同根的基础词。

entries.definition: relating to hearing
entries.definitionCN: 听觉的；同根形容词。

entries.definition: the place where people hear
entries.definitionCN: 听的场所；礼堂，同根。

entries.definition: bold, daring
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的；只是形近，词源与「听」无关。

entries.definition: a person who keeps or inspects financial records
entries.definitionCN: 会计；做账或查账的人，但不一定出具独立意见。

entries.definition: an official who checks that rules are followed
entries.definitionCN: 检查员；侧重实地查看，范围更宽。

entries.definition: a person who judges value or quality
entries.definitionCN: 评估员；侧重估价或评级。

entries.definition: a person who records daily transactions
entries.definitionCN: 记账员；只记录流水，不做独立核查。

normalIntro.en: Auditor is audit plus the agent ending -or: the person who does the hearing.
normalIntro.cn: auditor 就是 audit 加指人词尾 -or：做那场「听审」的人。

normal.en: The ending -or marks a doer, as in actor and doctor.
normal.cn: 词尾 -or 表示做事的人，如演员与医生。

normal.en: An external auditor comes from outside the firm.
normal.cn: 外部审计师来自公司之外。

normal.en: An internal auditor works inside the organization.
normal.cn: 内部审计员在机构内部工作。

normal.en: On campus an auditor listens but earns no credit.
normal.cn: 在校园里旁听生只听课、不拿学分。

normal.en: Auditor and auditory share the stem, not the meaning.
normal.cn: auditor 与 auditory 共用词干，意思却不同。

abstract.en: Picture a stranger with a pencil opposite the ledger.
abstract.cn: 想象一个陌生人拿着铅笔坐在账本对面。

abstract.en: Picture a tick appearing beside every second line.
abstract.cn: 想象每隔一行就出现一个钩。

abstract.en: Picture a back-row student with no exam paper.
abstract.cn: 想象后排一个没有试卷的学生。

examples.en: The auditor asked for the original invoices.
examples.cn: 审计师索要原始发票。

examples.en: Two auditors spent a week in the warehouse.
examples.cn: 两名审计师在仓库待了一周。

examples.en: He enrolled as an auditor and sat through every lecture.
examples.cn: 他以旁听生身份注册，听完了每一节课。

root: 拉丁语 audire「听」的分词词干 audit- 加指人词尾 -or，构成 auditor「听者」；因中世纪账目需口头宣读核对，转为查账人，十九世纪美国高校又用它指旁听生。

sensesIntro.en: One who hears: first a listener in a hall, then a checker of accounts and rules, then a student who only listens, and finally the firm itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「听的人」：先是厅堂里的听者，再是账目与规则的核查者，然后是只听课的学生，最后还可以指事务所本身。

a checker of rules and systems

latinIntro.en: Latin auditor, a hearer, stands beside auditus, auditorium and audientia in the same family.

definition_en: a large room or building where people sit to hear speeches, concerts or plays; the part of a theatre where the audience sits

scene: 开学典礼那天，全校师生挤进了那座老礼堂。The whole school gathered in the auditorium for the opening ceremony.
sceneCN: 这里 auditorium 是「礼堂、会堂」（第 1 个义项）；句意是全校师生聚集在礼堂举行开学典礼。

pos.zh: 名词：礼堂；观众席；演出厅

derivatives.zh: 同族指人名词：听者；审计师

senses.title: A hall for gatherings
senses.definition: a large room in a school or institution where people gather to hear speeches or performances
senses.definitionCN: 学校或机构里供人聚集听讲话或看演出的大厅
senses.example: The ceremony was moved to the main auditorium.
senses.exampleCN: 典礼改在主礼堂举行。
senses.why: The Latin ending -orium names a place, so the word literally means the place for hearing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词尾 -orium 表示场所，所以这个词字面意思就是「听的场所」。

senses.title: The seating area of a theatre
senses.definition: the part of a theatre where the audience sits, as opposed to the stage
senses.definitionCN: 剧场中观众就座的部分，与舞台相对
senses.example: The auditorium was dark while the stage was lit.
senses.exampleCN: 舞台亮着灯，观众席却一片黑。
senses.why: Inside a theatre the word narrows from the whole building to the half built for ears rather than for performers.
senses.whyCN: 在剧场内部，这个词从整栋建筑缩小到「为耳朵而建」的那一半，而不是为演员建的那一半。

senses.title: A performance building
senses.definition: a whole building designed for concerts, lectures or large public events
senses.definitionCN: 为音乐会、演讲或大型公共活动而建的整栋建筑
senses.example: The city built an auditorium beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市在河边建了一座演出厅。
senses.why: American cities named grand public halls with the word, so it grew from a room to a building.
senses.whyCN: 美国城市用这个词命名大型公共厅堂，于是它从「房间」长成了「整栋建筑」。

senses.title: A large lecture room
senses.definition: a big teaching room with rising rows of seats facing one speaker
senses.definitionCN: 座位逐排升高、朝向一位讲授者的大教室
senses.example: First-year lectures are held in the largest auditorium.
senses.exampleCN: 一年级的大课在最大的阶梯教室上。
senses.why: This keeps the original Latin university sense: a room where hearers sit before a reader.
senses.whyCN: 这保留了拉丁语最初的大学义：听者坐在朗读者面前的房间。

senses.title: The people in the hall
senses.definition: the audience itself, named after the space it occupies
senses.definitionCN: 以所在空间代指的听众整体
senses.example: The auditorium rose to its feet at the end.
senses.exampleCN: 结束时全场听众起立。
senses.why: A container word can stand for what it contains, so the hall becomes the people inside it.
senses.whyCN: 容器词可以代指其中所装之物，于是「厅」变成了「厅里的人」。

intro.en: Auditorium is the place noun of the hearing family: audit- plus -orium, a room built so that people can hear.
intro.cn: auditorium 是「听」词族的场所名词：audit- 加 -orium，一间为了让人听清而建的房间。

items.en: Audire meant to hear; its participle stem audit- carried the idea into nouns of place.
items.cn: audire 意为「听」，其分词词干 audit- 把这个意思带进了场所名词。

items.en: Auditor meant a hearer, and in a school it meant a student who sat and listened.
items.cn: auditor 意为「听者」，在学校语境里指坐着听讲的学生。

items.en: In Latin the word named a lecture room or school, the place where hearers sat.
items.cn: 在拉丁语中这个词指讲堂或学校，即听者就座的地方。

items.en: English borrowed it in the eighteenth century for a place designed for listening.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入，指专为「听」而设计的场所。

items.en: American cities built large public halls and called them auditoriums, widening the word from a room to a building.
items.cn: 美国城市兴建大型公共厅堂并这样称呼它们，词义从房间扩大到整栋建筑。

items.en: Today it also names the seating area of a theatre, opposite the stage, and by extension the audience itself.
items.cn: 如今它也指剧场中与舞台相对的观众席，并引申指全场听众。

note.en: The look-alike group is the hearing family; the near-meaning group sorts large spaces by what they are built for.
note.cn: 形近组是「听」词族；近义组按用途区分各种大型空间。

entries.definition: a hearer, or a checker of accounts
entries.definitionCN: 听者；查账的人，同根。

entries.definition: relating to hearing
entries.definitionCN: 听觉的；同根形容词。

entries.definition: an official check of accounts
entries.definitionCN: 审计；同根的基础词。

entries.definition: bold or reckless
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的；只是形近，词源不同。

entries.definition: a large room for meetings or meals
entries.definitionCN: 大厅；泛指大型房间，不强调「听」。

entries.definition: a building for plays, with stage and seating
entries.definitionCN: 剧院；包含舞台与观众席的整体。

entries.definition: a round space with rising seats around it
entries.definitionCN: 圆形剧场；座位环绕，词源与「听」无关。

entries.definition: a hall where a whole school or body meets
entries.definitionCN: 集会厅；强调聚集，而非声学设计。

normalIntro.en: Auditorium is audit- plus -orium: the place where hearing happens.
normalIntro.cn: auditorium 就是 audit- 加 -orium：发生「听」这件事的地方。

normal.en: The ending -orium marks a place, as in sanatorium.
normal.cn: 词尾 -orium 表示场所，如疗养院。

normal.en: In a theatre the auditorium faces the stage.
normal.cn: 在剧场里观众席与舞台相对。

normal.en: American use can mean a whole building.
normal.cn: 美式用法可以指整栋建筑。

normal.en: Both auditoriums and auditoria are plurals.
normal.cn: 两种复数形式都成立，后者更书面。

normal.en: Audience is the people; auditorium is the room.
normal.cn: 听众指人，礼堂指房间。

abstract.en: Picture rows of seats all leaning toward one voice.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排座位都朝一个声音倾去。

abstract.en: Picture a dark sea of faces below a lit stage.
abstract.cn: 想象亮舞台下一片暗色的脸海。

abstract.en: Picture sound reaching the very last row.
abstract.cn: 想象声音一直送到最后一排。

examples.en: The auditorium holds eight hundred people.
examples.cn: 这座礼堂能容纳八百人。

examples.en: We sat near the back of the auditorium.
examples.cn: 我们坐在观众席靠后的位置。

examples.en: Two new auditoria were added to the campus.
examples.cn: 校园里新增了两座礼堂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：audit「听」加 -orium「场所」——专门用来听的房子就是礼堂；剧场里听的那一片座位也是它。

root: 拉丁语 audire「听」的分词词干 audit- 加场所后缀 -orium，构成 auditorium「讲堂、听讲之处」；十八世纪进入英语，美式英语扩为大型演出厅，并指剧场观众席。

sensesIntro.en: A place for hearing grows from a school hall to a whole building, then narrows to the seating half of a theatre, and finally stands for the people in it.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「听的场所」从学校礼堂长成整栋建筑，又缩小为剧场的观众席那一半，最后代指坐在里面的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of seats facing one direction so a voice can reach the last row
core.cn: 核心意象：一排排座位朝着同一方向，让声音送到最后一排

branches.en: a school hall for ceremonies
the dark half facing the stage
branches.cn: 朝着舞台的暗色那一半

branches.en: a public building for concerts
a big lecture room with rising seats
branches.cn: 座位升高的阶梯大教室

branches.en: the hall standing for its people

intro.en: The place ending -orium joins the hearing stem; the same stem gives the person, the act and the adjective.
intro.cn: 场所词尾 -orium 接在「听」的词干上；同一词干还给出指人、指行为与指性质的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin auditorium meant a lecture room, from auditor, a hearer, from audire, to hear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 auditorium 意为讲堂，来自 auditor「听者」，再来自 audire「听」。

items.example: an auditor in the back row

latinEntries.example: Latin auditorium was a room for hearers.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语里这个词指听者所在的房间。

latinEntries.example: Auditor is the person inside the room.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个词指房间里的那个人。

latinEntries.example: Audire is the base of both.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个动词是两者的基础。

definition_zh: 听觉的；听的；听觉器官的；通过声音传达的；（古义）听众
definition_en: relating to the sense of hearing or to the organs and processes that make hearing possible; in older use, an audience
core_image: 声波撞上耳膜，一路传到大脑里被听懂
scene: 实验室里，孩子戴上耳机，只对声音作出反应。The test measures auditory memory rather than sight.
sceneCN: 这里 auditory 是「听觉感知的」（第 2 个义项）；句意是这项测试测的是听觉记忆而不是视觉。

pos.zh: 形容词：听觉的；听的
名词（古义）：听众；听众席

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀：在听觉上；通过听觉

senses.title: Relating to the sense of hearing
senses.definition: concerned with the ability to hear, as opposed to seeing or touching
senses.definitionCN: 与听的能力有关的，与视觉、触觉相对
senses.example: Dogs have a wider auditory range than people.
senses.exampleCN: 狗的听觉范围比人宽。
senses.why: The Latin adjective meant belonging to a hearer, so it labels the whole channel of the ear.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语形容词意为「属于听者的」，所以它标注的是耳朵这整条通道。

senses.title: Relating to how sound is processed
senses.titleCN: 听觉感知的（心理与认知）
senses.definition: concerned with the way the mind receives and interprets sound
senses.definitionCN: 与大脑接收并解释声音的方式有关的
senses.example: The child needs help with auditory processing.
senses.exampleCN: 这孩子在听觉处理方面需要帮助。
senses.why: Psychology took the word from the ear to the brain, naming what happens after the sound arrives.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把这个词从耳朵搬到大脑，用来指声音到达之后发生的事。

senses.title: Naming structures of ear and brain
senses.definition: used in anatomy for the parts that carry or handle sound
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学中用于指传递或处理声音的各部分
senses.example: The auditory nerve carries signals to the brain.
senses.exampleCN: 听神经把信号送到大脑。
senses.why: Anatomy needs a fixed label for each part of a pathway, and the hearing adjective supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学需要给通路上的每个部分一个固定标签，「听觉的」这个形容词正好承担此任。

senses.title: Delivered through sound
senses.definition: given as sound rather than as text or picture
senses.definitionCN: 以声音而非文字或图像给出的
senses.example: The alarm gives an auditory warning as well as a light.
senses.exampleCN: 这个警报除了亮灯还发出声音警示。
senses.why: From the organ the word shifts to the medium: what reaches the ear counts as auditory.
senses.whyCN: 词义从器官转向媒介：凡是到达耳朵的都算「听觉的」。

senses.title: An audience in older use
senses.definition: in older English, the body of people listening, or the place where they sit
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的英语里，指听的人群，或他们就座的地方
senses.example: The preacher addressed a large auditory.
senses.exampleCN: 布道者向一大群听众讲话。
senses.why: Before the adjective dominated, the same form served as a noun for the hearers themselves.
senses.whyCN: 在形容词用法占主导之前，同一形式曾作名词，指听者本身。

intro.en: Auditory is the adjective of the hearing family, straight from Latin auditorius, belonging to a hearer.
intro.cn: auditory 是「听」词族的形容词，直接来自拉丁语 auditorius「属于听者的」。

items.en: Audire meant to hear, and gave the participle stem audit-.
items.cn: audire 意为「听」，提供了分词词干 audit-。

items.en: Auditor named the hearer, the person the adjective belongs to.
items.cn: auditor 指听者，也就是这个形容词所归属的那个人。

items.en: Auditorius meant pertaining to a hearer or to hearing, and was used in learned prose.
items.cn: auditorius 意为「与听者或听有关的」，多用于学术文字。

items.en: English took the adjective in the fifteenth century for anything pertaining to hearing.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个形容词，用于一切与听有关的事物。

items.en: The noun use for an audience or a listening place is recorded in the sixteenth century, and later became rare.
items.cn: 作名词指听众或听讲场所的用法在十六世纪有记录，后来变得罕见。

items.en: Anatomy, psychology and audiology made the adjective technical, from the auditory canal to auditory processing disorder.
items.cn: 解剖学、心理学与听觉学把这个形容词术语化，从耳道一直到听觉处理障碍。

note.en: The look-alike group is the hearing family; the near-meaning group separates words about sound from words about the ear.
note.cn: 形近组是「听」词族；近义组把「关于声音」与「关于耳朵」的词分开。

entries.definition: a hearer, or a checker of accounts
entries.definitionCN: 听者；查账的人，同根。

entries.definition: a hall built for hearing
entries.definitionCN: 为听而建的厅堂，同根。

entries.definition: the sense of hearing, or a trial performance
entries.definitionCN: 听觉；试演，同根。

entries.definition: loud enough to be heard
entries.definitionCN: 听得见的；同根，但说的是声音够不够大。

entries.definition: relating to the ear or hearing
entries.definitionCN: 耳的；听觉的，与「口头的」一词同音，易混。

entries.definition: relating to sound and how it travels in a space
entries.definitionCN: 声学的；侧重声音的物理性质，而非耳朵。

entries.definition: relating to sound waves or their speed
entries.definitionCN: 声波的；声速的，多用于物理与工程。

entries.definition: the everyday noun for the sense of sound
entries.definitionCN: 听力；日常名词，而听觉的是其形容词对应。

normalIntro.en: Auditory is audit- plus -ory: belonging to hearing, whether the ear, the brain or the signal.
normalIntro.cn: auditory 就是 audit- 加 -ory：属于「听」的，无论是耳朵、大脑还是信号。

normal.en: The ending -ory means relating to, as in sensory.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ory 表示「与……有关」，如感官的。

normal.en: Auditory nerve and auditory cortex are fixed terms.
normal.cn: 听神经与听觉皮层是固定术语。

normal.en: Audible describes the sound; auditory describes the sense.
normal.cn: 听得见的描述声音，听觉的描述感官。

normal.en: Aural sounds like oral, so write carefully.
normal.cn: 表示「耳的」那个词与「口头的」同音，拼写要小心。

normal.en: Acoustic is about the room, auditory about the listener.
normal.cn: 声学词说的是房间，听觉词说的是听的人。

abstract.en: Picture a wave hitting the eardrum and turning into a signal.
abstract.cn: 想象一列波撞上耳膜，变成信号。

abstract.en: Picture a cable running from the ear to the brain.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线从耳朵通到大脑。

abstract.en: Picture a room where only sound, not light, carries the message.
abstract.cn: 想象一个只用声音而非光来传信的屋子。

examples.en: The auditory nerve was damaged by the infection.
examples.cn: 听神经因感染而受损。

examples.en: She learns better through auditory input.
examples.cn: 她通过听觉输入学得更好。

examples.en: The device gives an auditory signal every minute.
examples.cn: 这个装置每分钟发出一次声音信号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：audit「听」加 -ory「与……有关」——凡是归耳朵管的都叫听觉的：听神经、听觉记忆、声音提示。

root: 拉丁语 audire「听」经 auditor「听者」派生出 auditorius「属于听者的」，十五世纪进入英语作形容词；现代解剖学、心理学与听觉学把它固定为术语，古义名词指听众。

sensesIntro.en: Belonging to hearing: first the sense itself, then the processing in the mind, then the anatomical parts, then any message sent as sound, and once the listeners themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: 「属于听的」：先是感官本身，再是脑中的处理，然后是解剖部件，接着是任何以声音送出的信息，古义还指听者本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sound wave striking the eardrum and travelling on to be understood
core.cn: 核心意象：声波撞上耳膜，一路传到大脑被听懂

branches.en: the sense of hearing itself
how the mind handles sound
nerve, canal and cortex
a warning sent as sound
the listeners in older prose

intro.en: The ending -ory makes an adjective of relation; joined to the hearing stem it covers organs, processes and signals.
intro.cn: 词尾 -ory 构成表示关联的形容词；接在「听」的词干上，就能覆盖器官、过程与信号。

latinIntro.en: Latin auditorius belongs to auditor, a hearer, from audire; the same family gives auditorium and auditus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 auditorius 属于 auditor「听者」，来自 audire；同族还有 auditorium 与 auditus。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个形容词是直接来源。
这个名词提供「人」的部分。
这个动词是基础。

definition_zh: 增加；增大；扩充；增援；（音乐）增音
definition_en: to add to something so that it becomes larger or stronger
core_image: 一只木桶里的水被一勺一勺添到桶沿
scene: 预算本上原本够用的数字，被一行行新条目往后推。New staff were hired to augment the small team.
sceneCN: 这里指在原有基础上追加人手（第 1 个义项：在已有之物上增加）；句意为雇了新员工来扩充这个小团队。

pos.zh: 增加；增大；扩充；增强

senses.title: To add to what already exists
senses.definition: to make something larger by adding to it
senses.definitionCN: 通过添加使某物变大
senses.example: New staff were hired to augment the small team.
senses.exampleCN: 雇了新员工来扩充这个小团队。
senses.why: Augmentum came from augere, to increase, and the verb always assumes something already there to add to.
senses.whyCN: augmentum 出自 augere「增加」，这个动词总预设已有某物可供添加。

senses.title: To supplement income or resources
senses.definition: to add a second source so that a supply becomes sufficient
senses.definitionCN: 增加第二个来源，使供给变得充足
senses.example: She augmented her salary with evening teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 她用晚间教学补充薪水。
senses.why: The added part fills a gap rather than replacing the whole.
senses.whyCN: 添加的部分填补缺口，而不是替换整体。

senses.title: To strengthen a force
senses.definition: to add troops or equipment to an existing force
senses.definitionCN: 给现有力量增加兵员或装备
senses.example: Two companies were sent to augment the garrison.
senses.exampleCN: 派了两个连去增强驻军。
senses.why: Military language keeps the plain sense of adding men to a line.
senses.whyCN: 军事用语保留「往队列里添人」的平实义。

senses.title: To raise a dose or treatment
senses.definition: to increase the amount of a medicine or therapy
senses.definitionCN: 增加药物或治疗的用量
senses.example: The doctor augmented the dose after the first week.
senses.exampleCN: 第一周后医生增加了剂量。
senses.why: Medicine adds to a regimen rather than magnifying a signal.
senses.whyCN: 医学往方案里添加，而不是放大信号。

senses.title: To raise a musical interval
senses.definition: to widen a musical interval by a semitone
senses.definitionCN: 把音程扩大一个半音
senses.example: The theme is augmented in the second movement.
senses.exampleCN: 主题在第二乐章中被增音扩大。
senses.why: Music gave the old verb a precise measured addition.
senses.whyCN: 音乐给了这个旧动词一种精确可量的添加。

senses.title: A grammatical prefix
senses.definition: a prefix added to a verb in some older Indo-European languages
senses.definitionCN: 在一些古老印欧语言中加到动词前的附加成分
senses.example: Greek marks past time with an augment before the stem.
senses.exampleCN: 希腊语在词干前加增音来标记过去时。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word for an addition fixed to the front of a form.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借这个词，指固定在词形前端的附加成分。

senses.title: To add a factor of production
senses.definition: to increase labour, capital or another input
senses.definitionCN: 增加劳动力、资本或其他投入
senses.example: The firm augmented capital rather than labour.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业增加的是资本，而不是劳动力。
senses.why: Economics counts the addition as an input, not as intensity.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把这种添加算作投入，而不是强度。

senses.title: To lay extra information over reality
senses.definition: to add a layer of digital information to what is seen
senses.definitionCN: 在所见之物上添加一层数字信息
senses.example: The glasses augment the street with names and times.
senses.exampleCN: 这副眼镜在街景上叠加名称与时刻。
senses.why: Augmented reality keeps the additive sense: the world is not replaced, only enlarged.
senses.whyCN: 增强现实保留了「添加」义：世界没有被替换，只是被扩充。

intro.en: Augment comes from Latin augmentare, to increase, from augmentum, an increase, from augere, to make grow. The line is clear; the deeper root is usually connected with growth.
intro.cn: augment 来自拉丁 augmentare「增加」，出自 augmentum「增量」，再追到 augere「使增长」。线索清楚；更深词根一般与「生长」相关。

items.en: Augere meant to increase, enlarge or enrich, and it also lies behind auctor, the one who causes growth.
items.cn: augere 意为增加、扩大、使丰盛，也藏在 auctor「使事物生长者」背后。

items.en: Augmentum was the increase itself, the amount added to something already present.
items.cn: augmentum 指增量本身，即加到已有之物上的那一部分。

items.en: The verb turned the noun into an act of adding, used of troops, wealth and honour.
items.cn: 动词把名词变成「添加」的行为，用于军队、财富与荣誉。

items.en: English took the verb in the late Middle Ages; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期借入这个动词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Music and grammar borrowed the word for measured additions to intervals and verb stems.
items.cn: 音乐与语法学借这个词，指对音程与动词词干的定量添加。

items.en: Late twentieth-century computing added a digital layer and kept the word additive.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的计算技术添加了一层数字信息，仍保留「添加」义。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin growth stem; the second group names other ways of making something larger.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「增长」词干；第二组是使某物变大的其他近义说法。

entries.definition: The act of adding to something; the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物添加的行为；名词。

entries.definition: Having something added, as in augmented reality.
entries.definitionCN: 被添加了东西的，如增强现实。

entries.definition: Serving to increase or enlarge.
entries.definitionCN: 起增加或扩大作用的。

entries.definition: A sale where bids increase the price; from the same growth verb.
entries.definitionCN: 出价使价格上升的拍卖；出自同一「增长」动词。

entries.definition: One who causes something to come into being, from auctor.
entries.definitionCN: 使事物产生的人，出自 auctor。

entries.definition: To become or make greater in size or amount.
entries.definitionCN: 在规模或数量上变大。

entries.definition: To add something extra to fill a gap.
entries.definitionCN: 添加额外之物以补缺口。

entries.definition: To raise or push up quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 快速提高或推高。

entries.definition: To strengthen, especially a force or structure.
entries.definitionCN: 加强，尤指力量或结构。

entries.definition: To grow larger in extent or scope.
entries.definitionCN: 在范围或规模上变大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin growth verb, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「增长」动词、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Augere is to increase, and augmentum is the amount added.
normal.cn: augere 是增加，augmentum 是添进去的量。

normal.en: Auctor and auction come from the same growth verb.
normal.cn: auctor 与 auction 出自同一个「增长」动词。

normal.en: Augment adds to what is there; amplify makes what is there larger in effect.
normal.cn: augment 往已有之物里添，amplify 把已有之物的效果放大。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: augment income, augment the team, augmented reality.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：增加收入、扩充团队、增强现实。

normal.en: Music augments an interval, grammar augments a verb stem.
normal.cn: 音乐增大音程，语法学给动词词干加增音。

abstract.en: Augment is a bucket filled spoon by spoon until it reaches the rim.
abstract.cn: 增加是一勺一勺把桶添到桶沿。

abstract.en: The word never replaces; it always puts something beside what is already there.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不替换，总是把某物放到已有之物旁边。

abstract.en: Augmented reality is the old idea in glass: the street plus a layer of names.
abstract.cn: 增强现实是旧观念落在镜片上：街道之上多一层名字。

examples.en: The scholarship augmented his savings but did not cover the rent.
examples.cn: 奖学金补充了他的存款，却不够付房租。

examples.en: Volunteers augmented the thin staff at the shelter.
examples.cn: 志愿者补充了收容所单薄的人手。

examples.en: The second theme augments the first by a full tone.
examples.cn: 第二主题把第一主题整整扩大一个全音。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥格门特」——往桶里再添一格：增加

root: 拉丁 augmentare「增加」← augmentum「增量」← augere「使增长」。同族 auctor「使事物生长者」与 auction「竞价拍卖」都出 augere；英语中世纪晚期借入，确切首见年代不确定。音乐与语法学借指定量添加，现代又有增强现实义。与 amplify 的区别：augment 另行添加，amplify 放大已有之物。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all add something: to an existing whole, to a supply, a force, a dose, an interval, a verb stem, a capital stock, and a digital layer over the world.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在「添加」：向已有整体、供给、兵力、剂量、音程、动词词干、资本存量，以及现实之上的数字层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bucket filled one spoon at a time until the water reaches the rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只木桶被一勺一勺添到桶沿。

branches.en: THE ADDED PART: what is put beside an existing whole and a second source of supply.
branches.cn: 添加的部分：放在已有整体旁边之物，以及第二个供给来源。

branches.en: THE STRONGER STOCK: more troops in the line and more capital in the firm.
branches.cn: 更厚的存量：队列里更多兵员，企业里更多资本。

branches.en: THE RAISED DOSE: more medicine in the regimen.
branches.cn: 提高的剂量：方案里更多的药。

branches.en: THE MEASURED ADDITION: a wider interval and a prefix fixed to a verb.
branches.cn: 定量的添加：扩大的音程与加在动词前的成分。

branches.en: THE ADDED LAYER: digital information laid over the visible world.
branches.cn: 添加的层：铺在可见世界之上的数字信息。

intro.en: Augment is the Latin growth verb with its noun and participle; augere sits at the centre.
intro.cn: augment 是拉丁「增长」动词及其名词、分词形式；中心是 augere。

latinIntro.en: Augere supplies growth, augmentum the amount added, and augmentare the act of adding.
latinIntro.cn: augere 提供「增长」，augmentum 提供「添加的量」，augmentare 提供「添加」的行为。

items.exampleCN: 同一词干命名使事物产生的人。

definition_zh: 朴素的；严峻的；苦行的；简朴无饰的
definition_en: deliberately plain and without ornament, or strict and severe in manner or conditions
core_image: 一间石屋，只有木桌、木凳和一盏灯，墙面空得能听见回声
scene: 山中的小屋只有一张木桌、一盏灯，墙上没有任何装饰。The monks live an austere life with few possessions.
sceneCN: 这里 austere 指生活朴素、没有装饰与奢侈品（第 1 个义项：朴素无饰）；句意为僧侣们过着几乎没有财物的简朴生活。

pos.zh: 朴素的；严峻的；苦行的

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

senses.title: Plain and without ornament
senses.definition: deliberately simple, with no decoration and no unnecessary comfort
senses.definitionCN: 刻意简单，没有装饰，也没有多余的舒适
senses.example: The monks live an austere life with few possessions.
senses.exampleCN: 僧侣们过着几乎没有财物的简朴生活。
senses.why: The Greek word meant 'dry, harsh': anything stripped of moisture is also stripped of softness, and a room can be described the same way.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词意为「干燥、粗硬」：被抽去水分的东西也被抽去柔软，房间也可以用同样的方式描述。

senses.title: Severe in manner
senses.definition: strict and serious in manner, allowing no warmth or lightness
senses.definitionCN: 举止严格而严肃，不容温暖或轻快
senses.example: The headmaster gave an austere welcome and then listed the rules.
senses.exampleCN: 校长作了严峻的欢迎，随后列出各项规定。
senses.why: A person who refuses ornament in a room often refuses it in behaviour too, so plainness becomes a social style.
senses.whyCN: 一个在房间里拒绝装饰的人，往往在行为上也拒绝装饰，于是朴素变成一种社交风格。

senses.title: Morally strict
senses.definition: holding to a disciplined moral code, often with a religious basis
senses.definitionCN: 恪守严格纪律化的道德准则，常带宗教基础
senses.example: The order was known for its austere discipline.
senses.exampleCN: 这个修会以严苛的戒律闻名。
senses.why: Moral strictness borrows the image of a bare room: fewer comforts are believed to leave more attention for what matters.
senses.whyCN: 道德严格借用了空房间的意象：更少的舒适被认为能给要紧之事留下更多注意力。

senses.title: A bare place
senses.definition: of a place, cold, bare and lacking in softness or colour
senses.definitionCN: 指场所冷清、空旷，缺少柔软与色彩
senses.example: The hospital corridor was austere and brightly lit.
senses.exampleCN: 医院的走廊空荡冷清，灯光明亮。
senses.why: Architecture uses the word for spaces that refuse to comfort the body, so the eye finds nowhere soft to rest.
senses.whyCN: 建筑学用这个词指拒绝让身体舒适的空间，于是目光找不到柔软之处停留。

senses.title: Harshly restrictive policy
senses.definition: of economic policy, harshly restrictive, cutting spending and comfort
senses.definitionCN: 指经济政策严厉受限，削减开支与福利
senses.example: The government adopted austere measures after the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机之后政府采取了紧缩措施。
senses.why: A national budget can be stripped the way a room is stripped: the ornaments go first, then the necessities are questioned.
senses.whyCN: 国家预算可以像房间一样被清空：先去掉装饰，接着连必需品也受到质疑。

senses.title: A restrained style
senses.definition: of art, music or writing, stripped of ornament and easy emotion
senses.definitionCN: 指艺术、音乐或写作去掉装饰与轻易的情感
senses.example: Her austere prose leaves every word exposed.
senses.exampleCN: 她克制的文笔让每个词都裸露在外。
senses.why: Style can practise the same denial as a room: what is removed makes the remaining shapes more visible.
senses.whyCN: 风格可以像房间一样实践这种舍弃：被移走的东西让剩下的形状更显眼。

senses.title: Beauty from bareness
senses.definition: a beauty that comes from bareness and proportion rather than decoration
senses.definitionCN: 源于空净与比例而非装饰的美
senses.example: The chapel is admired for its austere beauty.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小教堂以其素净之美受人赞赏。
senses.why: When ornament is gone, proportion must carry the whole effect, and that is the beauty the word praises.
senses.whyCN: 装饰消失后，比例必须承担全部效果，这正是这个词所赞赏的美。

senses.title: Deliberate self-denial
senses.definition: the practice of denying oneself comfort or pleasure for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某个目的而刻意放弃舒适或享乐的做法
senses.example: His austerity was a protest against wasteful display.
senses.exampleCN: 他的自我节制是对铺张炫耀的一种抗议。
senses.why: Self-denial turns plainness into a choice: the bare room is not a lack but a statement.
senses.whyCN: 自我节制把朴素变成选择：空房间不是匮乏，而是一种声明。

intro.en: Austere goes back to a Greek word for dry and harsh, and entered English through Latin.
intro.cn: austere 可追溯到希腊语中表示「干燥、粗硬」的词，经拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The root behind the Greek adjective is connected with dryness, the idea that makes a dry thing stiff and unbending.
items.cn: 希腊语形容词背后的词根与「干燥」有关，正是干燥使东西僵硬、不易弯曲。

items.en: Greek austeros meant dry and harsh, and was used of wind, taste and character alike.
items.cn: 希腊语 austeros 意为「干燥、粗硬」，风、味道与性格都可以用它形容。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as austerus, harsh, dry or sour, describing things that pucker the mouth; the noun austeritas named the quality.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 austerus，意为「粗硬、干燥、酸涩」，描述让嘴收缩的东西；名词 austeritas 指这种性质。

items.en: English took the adjective in the fourteenth century for harsh taste and for a strict, self-denying life.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个形容词，用于粗涩的味道与严格克己的生活。

items.en: Writers on art and building then used it for work stripped of ornament, where bareness itself became a virtue.
items.cn: 此后谈论艺术与建筑的作者用它形容去掉装饰的作品，素净本身成了一种优点。

items.en: In modern politics the related noun names cuts in public spending, while in design it still praises plainness.
items.cn: 在现代政治中，相关名词指削减公共开支；在设计领域，它仍赞赏朴素。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same stem; the near-meaning group names other kinds of plainness and severity.
note.cn: 形近组共享同一词干；近义组列出其他形式的朴素与严峻。

entries.definitionCN: 朴素，或严厉削减开支的政策。

entries.definition: in a plain or severe manner.

entries.definition: practices of self-denial or official cutbacks.

entries.definitionCN: 一组中最朴素或最严峻的；这一形式罕用，现代英语通常说 most austere。

entries.definition: very strict or harsh, without gentleness.
entries.definitionCN: 非常严格或严酷，不带温和。

entries.definition: simple and harsh, allowing no luxury.

entries.definition: plain and harsh in appearance, with no softening detail.
entries.definitionCN: 外观朴素严酷，没有柔化细节。

entries.definition: careful with money and resources, avoiding waste.

normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「只有一盏灯的空房间」这一画面留住。

normal.en: Picture a stone room with one table and one lamp; the missing furniture is the word.
normal.cn: 想象一间石屋，只有一桌一灯；缺席的家具就是这个词。

normal.en: Austere and 'austerity' share a stem: both mean cutting away the extra.
normal.cn: austere 与 austerity 同词干：两者都表示把多余的东西切掉。

normal.en: Dryness makes a thing stiff; a dry style is stiff and unbending too.
normal.cn: 干燥使东西僵硬；干燥的风格也僵硬而不弯。

normal.en: Say aw-STEER, as if steering away from comfort.
normal.cn: 读成 aw-STEER，好像在把方向转离舒适。

normal.en: Link it with spartan: both describe lives with few possessions.
normal.cn: 把它和 spartan 联系：两者都描述财物很少的生活。

abstract.cn: 去掉装饰后，比例必须承担美感。

abstract.en: A bare room can be a statement rather than a lack.
abstract.cn: 空房间可以是声明，而不只是匮乏。

abstract.en: The same word serves art, architecture and national budgets because all three can be stripped.
abstract.cn: 同一个词适用于艺术、建筑与国家预算，因为三者都可以被剥净。

sensesIntro.en: Austere always means something has been stripped away; the senses differ in whether what is removed is ornament, comfort, spending or softness of manner.
sensesIntro.cn: austere 始终表示某物被剥去了一层；各义项的差别在于被去掉的是装饰、舒适、开支还是举止中的柔软。

branches.en: Plain rooms and plain lives with few objects.
branches.cn: 陈设极少的房间与生活。

branches.en: Severity of behaviour and of moral discipline.
branches.cn: 行为与道德纪律上的严峻。

branches.en: A national budget cut to the bone.

intro.en: The word is a Greek adjective that came through Latin, and its family keeps the idea of dryness and strictness.
intro.cn: 这个词是经拉丁语而来的希腊形容词，其同族词保留「干燥」与「严格」的概念。

definition_zh: 紧缩；节俭，清苦；朴素，无装饰；严峻；艰苦时期；苦行
definition_en: the quality of being plain and without comfort or ornament; strict economy in spending, especially by a government; a practice of self-denial
core_image: 把装饰与多余的东西一件件拿走，只剩必需
scene: 危机之后，政府砍掉补贴，公共开支一路收紧。The government defended austerity as a way to cut the deficit.
sceneCN: 这里 austerity 是「财政紧缩」（第 1 个义项）；句意是政府为削减赤字而为紧缩政策辩护。

pos.zh: 名词：紧缩；节俭；朴素；严峻；苦行

derivatives.zh: 同族形容词：朴素的；严峻的
加副词后缀：朴素地；严峻地
