senses.title: Strict cuts in public spending
senses.definition: a government policy of reducing spending and borrowing, usually after a crisis
senses.definitionCN: 政府削减开支与借贷的政策，通常在危机之后推行
senses.example: Austerity reduced the deficit but closed two libraries.
senses.exampleCN: 紧缩降低了赤字，却关掉两座图书馆。
senses.why: The old sense of harsh self-denial was applied to a state: the country must live on less, as a monk does.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「克己受苦」义被用到国家身上：国家也得像修士那样少花少用。

senses.title: Plain living without comfort
senses.definition: a way of living that allows no luxury and few comforts
senses.definitionCN: 不容奢侈、少有舒适的生活方式
senses.example: They chose austerity for the sake of the work.
senses.exampleCN: 为了工作，他们选择了清苦的生活。
senses.why: Dryness becomes a moral choice: what is stripped away is pleasure, not necessity.
senses.whyCN: 「干涩」变成一种道德选择：被抽掉的是享受，而不是必需。

senses.title: Absence of ornament
senses.definition: the quality of a design or style that uses no decoration
senses.definitionCN: 设计或风格不加装饰的性质
senses.example: The austerity of the chapel suits the landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 小教堂的素净与这片风景相称。
senses.why: What is dry and bare in taste becomes bare in appearance, and bareness can be praised as honesty.
senses.whyCN: 味道上的干涩转到外观上的光秃，而这种光秃可以被赞为诚实。

senses.title: Severity of manner
senses.definition: a strict, unsmiling manner that shows no softness
senses.definitionCN: 严格、不带笑意、毫无柔和的态度
senses.example: The austerity of his face frightened new students.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上的严峻让新生害怕。
senses.why: A person who denies himself comfort often denies others warmth, so the word moves from things to faces.
senses.whyCN: 对自己不给舒适的人，往往对别人也不给温和，于是这个词从物品转到面孔。

senses.title: Hard conditions of a period
senses.definition: the harsh conditions of a time when goods and money are short, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 物资与钱款短缺时期的艰苦状况，常用复数
senses.example: The austerities of the war years shaped her habits.
senses.exampleCN: 战争年代的匮乏塑造了她的习惯。
senses.why: When hardship is imposed rather than chosen, the plural names the separate privations people endured.
senses.whyCN: 当艰苦是被强加而非自选时，复数形式指人们挨过的一桩桩匮乏。

senses.title: Religious self-denial
senses.definition: a practice of fasting or bodily discipline undertaken for spiritual reasons, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 出于精神目的而进行的斋戒或身体磨炼，通常用复数
senses.example: Lenten austerities included fasting and silence.
senses.exampleCN: 四旬期的苦行包括斋戒与静默。
senses.why: This is the oldest English use: the dry, harsh life chosen to train the soul.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最老的用法：为磨炼灵魂而自选的干涩严苦生活。

intro.en: Austerity comes from a Greek word for dry and harsh, through Latin; what dries the mouth became what strips away comfort.
intro.cn: austerity 出自希腊语表示「干燥、粗硬」的词，经拉丁语而来；让嘴发干的东西，变成了抽走舒适的东西。

items.en: Greek austeros meant dry and harsh, used of wind, taste and character; the root behind it is connected with dryness.
items.cn: 希腊语 austeros 意为「干燥、粗硬」，风、味道与性格都能用；其背后的词根与「干燥」有关。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as austerus, harsh, dry or sour, describing what puckers the mouth.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 austerus，意为「粗硬、干燥、酸涩」，描述让嘴收缩的东西。

items.en: The noun austeritas named the quality of harshness or strictness.
items.cn: 名词 austeritas 指粗硬或严格这种性质。

items.en: Old French austérité carried the noun into the western languages in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 austérité 在十四世纪把这个名词带入西欧语言。

items.en: English took the word for severity of life and manner, especially the self-denial of religious discipline.
items.cn: 英语借入后指生活与态度的严苦，尤其是宗教修行中的克己。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became a political term for cuts in public spending, while design still uses it for plainness.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词成为削减公共开支的政治术语，而设计领域仍用它指朴素。

note.en: The look-alike group mixes the true family with two words that only share the ending; the near-meaning group grades thrift and harshness.
note.cn: 形近组把真正的同族词与两个只是词尾相同的词放在一起；近义组按节约与严酷的程度分级。

entries.definition: plain, severe, without comfort
entries.definitionCN: 朴素的；严峻的；同族形容词。

entries.definition: in a plain or severe manner
entries.definitionCN: 朴素地；严峻地；同族副词。

entries.definition: all future generations
entries.definitionCN: 后代；只是词尾音近，词源无关。

entries.definition: the state of being wealthy and successful
entries.definitionCN: 繁荣；词尾相同但词源不同，意义上正好相反。

entries.definition: careful use of money, without the sense of hardship
entries.definitionCN: 节俭；侧重不浪费，不含被迫受苦之意。

entries.definition: careful management of money as a virtue
entries.definitionCN: 节约；日常理财美德，语气温和。

entries.definition: cutting costs inside an organization
entries.definitionCN: 削减开支；多用于机构内部，政治色彩较弱。

entries.definition: harshness of manner or conditions
entries.definitionCN: 严峻；侧重态度或条件的严酷，不涉及花钱。

normalIntro.en: Austerity is the noun of austere: dryness turned into a way of living, a style and a policy.
normalIntro.cn: austerity 是 austere 的名词：把「干涩」变成生活方式、风格与政策。

normal.en: The ending -ity turns an adjective into a quality.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ity 把形容词变成性质名词。

normal.en: Austerity measures is the fixed political phrase.
normal.cn: 紧缩措施是固定的政治搭配。

normal.en: The plural austerities means acts of self-denial.
normal.cn: 复数形式指一桩桩苦行。

normal.en: Austere describes things; austerity names the state.
normal.cn: 形容词描述事物，名词指那种状态。

normal.en: Prosperity only shares the ending, not the root.
normal.cn: 繁荣一词只是词尾相同，词根无关。

abstract.en: Picture a room from which every ornament is carried out.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，装饰被一件件搬走。

abstract.en: Picture a budget with whole lines crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象一份预算，整行整行被划掉。

abstract.en: Picture a dry mouth that refuses the sweet wine.
abstract.cn: 想象一张干涩的嘴，拒绝那杯甜酒。

examples.en: Austerity shaped the design of the whole building.
examples.cn: 朴素的取向决定了整栋建筑的设计。

examples.en: The government imposed austerity after the crisis.
examples.cn: 危机之后政府推行了紧缩。

examples.en: The austerities of the monastery included silence at meals.
examples.cn: 修道院的苦行包括用餐时静默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「干涩」：把水分、装饰与享受都抽干，剩下的就是紧缩、清苦与严峻。

root: 希腊语 austeros「干燥、粗硬」经拉丁语 austerus 与 austeritas、古法语 austérité 进入英语；由「让嘴发干的粗涩」引申为生活清苦、风格朴素、态度严峻，二十世纪又指财政紧缩。

sensesIntro.en: Dryness becomes a policy, a way of life, a style, a face, a hard period and a spiritual discipline.
sensesIntro.cn: 「干涩」依次变成政策、生活方式、风格、面孔、艰苦时期与精神修行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ornaments and comforts carried out one by one until only the necessary remains
core.cn: 核心意象：装饰与舒适被一件件搬走，只剩必需

branches.en: a state cutting its spending
a life without luxury
a bare chapel wall
an unsmiling face
hard years and chosen discipline
branches.cn: 艰苦的岁月与自选的修行

intro.en: The stem auster- means dry and harsh; the noun ending -ity names the quality, and -ly makes the adverb.
intro.cn: 词干 auster- 意为「干燥、粗硬」；名词词尾 -ity 指这种性质，-ly 构成副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin austerus and austeritas carry the Greek stem into English; the deeper root is linked with dryness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 austerus 与 austeritas 把希腊词干带进英语；更深的词根与「干燥」有关。

items.meaning: in a plain or severe way

items.exampleCN: 拉丁语的「粗硬」与「粗硬之性」

latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个词曾形容风与味道。
这是拉丁语的借入形式。
这个名词产生了英语的对应词。

definition_zh: 真正的；真迹的；地道的；正宗的；可信的；真诚的；权威的（古义）；有法律效力的；原真的
definition_en: coming from the source it claims to come from, and therefore real, reliable, or faithful to an original
core_image: 一只手在旧画角落找到画家的签名——不是像，而是本人留下的那一笔
scene: 厨房里蒸汽升腾，一位厨师对来客轻声开口。A chef tells a visitor: This is an authentic recipe, copied by hand from my grandmother's notebook.
sceneCN: 这里 authentic 指「地道的、正宗的」（第 2 个义项：照着原产地做法）；句意：这是一份地道的食谱，是从我祖母的笔记本上亲手抄下来的。画面里有手写食谱、面粉和一口旧锅。

pos.zh: 真正的；真迹的；地道的；可信的；真诚的

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

senses.title: Real, not false
senses.definition: real and not false, invented, or imitated
senses.definitionCN: 真实而非虚假、编造或仿制的
senses.example: The museum bought the letter only after proving it authentic.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆在证明这封信为真迹之后才买下它。
senses.why: Greek authentikos meant 'original, principal', from authentes 'one who acts on his own authority'. A genuine thing is one that can stand as its own source, not a copy of another.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 authentikos 意为「原初的、主要的」，出自 authentes「凭自己权威行事者」。真正的东西能作为自身的来源站住，而不是另一个东西的复制。

senses.title: Of the original place
senses.definition: made or done in the original regional way
senses.definitionCN: 按原地区的做法制作或进行的
senses.example: She learned to cook authentic Sichuan food in Chengdu.
senses.exampleCN: 她在成都学会了做地道的川菜。
senses.why: Once the source is a place rather than a person, 'original' means 'as done there'. The adjective moves from legal proof to cultural fidelity.
senses.whyCN: 一旦来源从一个人变成一个地方，「原初」就变成「照着那里做」。这个形容词从法律证明滑向了文化忠实。

senses.title: Worthy of belief
senses.titleCN: 可信的：对得上发生的事
senses.definition: of an account or report, deserving to be believed
senses.definitionCN: （叙述或报道）值得相信的
senses.example: The book gives an authentic account of life in the trenches.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对战壕生活作了可信的记述。
senses.why: Mid-14th-century English also recorded 'real, entitled to acceptance as factual'. The word judges a statement's correspondence to what happened, so 'reliable' became its natural neighbour.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪中叶的英语还记录了「真实的、可被接受为事实的」义。这个词判断陈述与已发生之事的对应关系，所以 reliable 成了它的天然邻居。

senses.title: From the maker's own hand
senses.definition: being the original work, not a reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 是原作而非复制品的
senses.example: Only an authentic signature adds value to the print.
senses.exampleCN: 只有真迹签名才会给这幅版画增值。
senses.why: The legal document model — this is the very instrument, sealed by its maker — was transferred to art. The adjective then answers 'whose hand made this?'
senses.whyCN: 法律文书的模型——就是这一份，由制作者盖印——被移到艺术上。这个形容词于是回答「这是谁的手做的？」

senses.title: Sincere, not performed
senses.definition: of a person or feeling, sincere and not performed for an audience
senses.definitionCN: （人或情感）真诚而不为观众表演的
senses.example: His surprise seemed authentic, not staged for the cameras.
senses.exampleCN: 他的惊讶看起来是真的，不是为镜头摆拍的。
senses.why: The existential sense of 'own' rather than 'copied' became a moral one: an authentic feeling belongs to the person who shows it. The word now praises the absence of pretence.
senses.whyCN: 「属于自己的」而非「抄来的」这一存在主义义变成道德义：真实的情感属于显露它的人。这个词如今称赞的是「没有伪装」。

senses.title: Authoritative, in older use
senses.titleCN: 权威的：古义里的「正式授权」
senses.definition: authoritative or duly authorized, an older sense now rare
senses.definitionCN: 有权威或经正式授权的，此为现已罕见的旧义
senses.example: The decree was authentic because the king's seal was on it.
senses.exampleCN: 这道敕令是正式有效的，因为上面有国王的印章。
senses.why: This was the word's first English sense, from Medieval Latin authenticus, translating Greek authentikos. Authority and authenticity were one idea before truth separated them.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最早的英语义，来自中世纪拉丁语 authenticus，是对希腊语 authentikos 的翻译。在「真」把两者分开之前，权威与真实原本是一个概念。

senses.title: Legally valid
senses.definition: executed in the proper legal form, so as to be valid
senses.definitionCN: 按正当法律形式作成因而有效的
senses.example: An authentic will must be signed before two witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 一份有法律效力的遗嘱必须在两名见证人面前签署。
senses.why: Latin authenticus named documents that could be enforced. The adjective still appears in legal phrases where formal execution, not sincerity, is what counts.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 authenticus 指可被强制执行的文件。这个形容词仍出现在法律短语里，在那里算数的是正式作成，而不是真诚。

senses.title: Faithful to a period
senses.titleCN: 原真的：复原到原来的演法
senses.definition: reproducing the original style, instruments, or materials of a period
senses.definitionCN: 复现某一时期的原风格、原乐器或原材料的
senses.example: The ensemble performs authentic Baroque music on gut strings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个乐团用羊肠弦演奏原真的巴洛克音乐。
senses.why: The question 'is this the original?' becomes a programme: reconstruct period practice. 'Authentic performance' is a claim about method, not about a single surviving object.
senses.whyCN: 「这是不是原件」这个问题变成了一套方法：复原当时的做法。authentic performance 是对方法的宣称，而不是对某件幸存实物的宣称。

senses.title: Firmly evidenced
senses.definition: of evidence, firmly established and not merely probable
senses.definitionCN: （证据）确凿成立、不只是可能的
senses.example: Police need authentic evidence, not a rumour from the street.
senses.exampleCN: 警方需要确凿的证据，而不是街头的传言。
senses.why: From 'entitled to acceptance as factual', the adjective hardens into an evidential standard. What is authentic has a source that can be produced and checked.
senses.whyCN: 从「可被接受为事实」出发，这个形容词硬化为一条证据标准。真实的东西有一个可以拿出来、可以核查的来源。

intro.en: Authentic arrived in English as a word about authority and only later settled into a word about truth. Its Greek ancestor names a person who acts on his own authority; a document, an object, or a feeling is authentic when it can claim that kind of source.
intro.cn: authentic 初到英语时讲的是权威，后来才落定为讲「真」的词。它的希腊祖先指「凭自己权威行事的人」；一份文件、一件物品或一种情感，只要能声称有那样的来源，就是 authentic。

items.en: authentikos 'original, genuine, principal' came from authentes 'one acting on one's own authority', autos 'self' + hentes 'doer, being'. The root behind hentes, PIE *sene- (2) 'to accomplish', is reconstructed, with no written record, so it is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: authentikos「原初的、真正的、主要的」出自 authentes「凭自己权威行事者」，即 autos「自己」+ hentes「行事者、存在者」。hentes 背后的词根 PIE *sene- (2)「完成」是重构形式，没有书面记录，标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: authenticus carried the Greek adjective into Latin, where it attached to documents, seals and authorities. The word certified a source before it described a fact.
items.cn: authenticus 把希腊形容词带进拉丁语，在那里附着于文件、印章与权威。这个词先证明来源，后来才描述事实。

items.en: autentique 'authentic; canonical' (Modern French authentique) entered English through Norman and central French, losing the Greek -h- on the way.
items.cn: autentique「真正的；正典的」（现代法语 authentique）经诺曼法语与中部法语进入英语，一路丢掉了希腊语的 h。

items.en: autentik is recorded as 'authoritative, duly authorized' and, in the same century, as 'real, entitled to acceptance as factual'. The -th- spelling was restored later by learned reference to Latin and Greek.
items.cn: autentik 被记录为「有权威的、经正式授权的」，同一世纪也指「真实的、可被接受为事实的」。后来学者参照拉丁语和希腊语，把 -th- 的拼写补了回来。

items.en: The factual sense won: authentic came to mean 'real, not fictitious', while genuine stressed that the reputed author is the real one. OED notes that the 18th-century distinction is not etymological.
items.cn: 「符合事实」义胜出：authentic 指「真实、非虚构」，而 genuine 强调所署作者确为其人。OED 指出，18 世纪的那套区分并不符合词源。

items.en: Authentic extended to regional food, heritage sites, the 'authentic self', and historically informed performance, so that fidelity to an origin became a value in its own right.
items.cn: authentic 扩展到地方饮食、文化遗产地、「真实的自我」和历史复原演奏，对来源的忠实本身成了一种价值。

note.en: The first group shares the authent- stem or the -entic sound; the second group names things that are real or believable, which authentic can mean in different contexts.
note.cn: 第一组共享 authent- 词干或 -entic 读音；第二组是「真」或「可信」的近义词，authentic 在不同语境下可以对应它们。

entries.definition: the quality of being genuine or trustworthy. It is authentic plus -ity, the abstract noun.
entries.definitionCN: 真实性；真品性。它是 authentic 加 -ity 构成的抽象名词。

entries.definition: in a genuine, original, or sincere way.
entries.definitionCN: 真实地；地道地；真诚地。

entries.definition: the process of proving that something or someone is genuine.
entries.definitionCN: 认证；鉴定；身份验证。

entries.definition: not genuine; imitated or performed.
entries.definitionCN: 不真实的；伪造的；造作的。

entries.definition: the creator of a work, from Latin auctor. The sound is close, the family is not.
entries.definitionCN: 作者；创作者，出自拉丁语 auctor。读音相近，词族不同。

entries.definition: real and exactly what it is said to be, especially of a person's feelings or an object's origin.
entries.definitionCN: 真正的；名副其实的，尤指情感或物品来源。

entries.definition: actually existing or happening, not imagined or pretended. It is the plain word behind authentic.
entries.definitionCN: 真实的；实际存在的。它是 authentic 背后那个朴素的词。

entries.definition: existing from the beginning, or being the first version rather than a copy.
entries.definitionCN: 最初的；原作的；非复制的。

entries.definition: convincing enough to be believed. It matches authentic in the 'reliable account' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 可信的；有说服力的。对应 authentic 的「可信记述」义。

entries.definition: allowed by law or by the rules, or reasonable and genuine. It covers authentic's legal and sincere edges.
entries.definitionCN: 合法的；正当的；合理的。它覆盖 authentic 的法律义与真诚义边缘。

normalIntro.en: authent- is the Greek stem for 'acting on one's own authority'; -ic makes it an adjective. The whole family turns on who has the right to speak for a thing.
normalIntro.cn: authent- 是希腊语「凭自己权威行事」的词干；-ic 使它成为形容词。整个词族都围绕「谁有权为某物作证」。

normal.en: authentic = author-like: both suggest someone standing behind the thing, though the two words are not related.
normal.cn: authentic 与 author 形似：都暗示有一个「人」站在东西背后，不过两词并不同源。

normal.en: An authentic signature is a signature you can put under a microscope.
normal.cn: authentic signature 是一枚可以放到显微镜下查验的签名。

normal.en: authentic food tastes of the place, not of the airport.
normal.cn: authentic 的食物有那个地方的味道，而不是机场的味道。

normal.en: Authentic and genuine are siblings in use: genuine asks whose hand, authentic asks what warrant.
normal.cn: authentic 与 genuine 是用法上的兄弟：genuine 问「谁的手」，authentic 问「什么凭证」。

normal.en: The -th- is a learned repair: French left it out, English put it back from the Latin.
normal.cn: 中间的 -th- 是一次学术修补：法语漏掉了它，英语照拉丁语补回。

abstract.en: The word begins as a seal and ends as a feeling: authority moved from the document to the person.
abstract.cn: 这个词从一枚印章开始，到一种情感结束：权威从文件移到了人身上。

abstract.en: Authentic always compares two things: the copy and the source it claims to come from.
abstract.cn: authentic 永远在比较两样东西：复制品，以及它声称来自的来源。

abstract.en: To call a thing authentic is to accept a chain of custody, even when the chain is only a recipe.
abstract.cn: 称某物 authentic，就是接受一条来源链，哪怕这条链只是一份食谱。

examples.en: The dealer could not prove that the vase was authentic.
examples.cn: 经销商无法证明这只花瓶是真品。

examples.en: We wanted an authentic meal, so we ate where the drivers eat.
examples.cn: 我们想吃一顿地道的饭，于是去了司机们吃饭的地方。

examples.en: Her anger was authentic and passed in a minute.
examples.cn: 她的愤怒是真的，一分钟就过去了。

dict_mnemonic.text: authentic 拆成 author（作者）+ tic——作者亲手交出的一笔，当然是「真迹的、真正的」

root: 源自希腊语 authentikos「原初的、真正的、主要的」← authentes「凭自己权威行事者」（autos「自己」+ hentes「行事者」），经拉丁语 authenticus 与古法语 autentique 进入英语；核心是「有一只手或一个来源为它作证」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses answer one question in different rooms: a letter, a kitchen, a courtroom, a gallery, a diary, a concert. In each, authentic asks whether the thing comes from the hand or place it claims.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项在不同房间里回答同一个问题：一封书信、一间厨房、一座法庭、一间画廊、一本日记、一场音乐会。每个场景里，authentic 都在问：这东西是否出自它声称的那只手或那个地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the maker's own hand, leaving a mark that a copy cannot leave.
core.cn: 核心意象：制作者本人的手，留下复制品留不下的痕迹。

branches.en: REAL AND VALID: a thing that is what it claims to be, and an instrument legally executed.
branches.cn: 真实与有效：名副其实的东西，以及依法作成的文书。

branches.en: TRUSTWORTHY: an account that fits the facts, and evidence firm enough to stand on.
branches.cn: 可信：与事实相符的叙述，以及足以站住的证据。

branches.en: ORIGINAL IN PLACE AND HAND: food cooked the local way, and a work from the maker's own hand.
branches.cn: 地方与手上的原初：按当地做法烹制的食物，以及出自本人之手的作品。

branches.en: THE SINCERE AND THE AUTHORIZED: a feeling that belongs to its bearer, and an old sense of official authority.
branches.cn: 真诚与授权：属于本人的情感，以及官方权威的旧义。

branches.en: FIDELITY TO A PERIOD: performance or restoration that follows the original practice.
branches.cn: 对时代的忠实：遵循原初做法的演出或修复。

intro.en: authentic is authent- (Greek authentes, 'one acting on his own authority') + -ic (adjective). Its family shows -ity, -ly, -ate, -ation, -or, and the negative prefix in-; author is a look-alike from Latin auctor, not a relative.
intro.cn: authentic 是 authent-（希腊语 authentes「凭自己权威行事者」）+ -ic（形容词）。词族展示 -ity、-ly、-ate、-ation、-or 以及否定前缀 in-；author 是出自拉丁语 auctor 的形近词，并非同族。

latinIntro.en: Greek authentikos gave Latin authenticus; authenticare 'to make valid' gave authenticate; -icus and -itat- are the suffixes behind English -ic and -ity.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 authentikos 给出拉丁语 authenticus；authenticare「使有效」给出 authenticate；-icus 与 -itat- 是英语 -ic 与 -ity 背后的后缀。

items.example: The document is authentic, not a nineteenth-century copy.
items.exampleCN: 这份文件是真件，不是 19 世纪的复制品。

items.example: The authenticity of the relic is disputed.
items.exampleCN: 这件圣物的真伪有争议。

items.meaning: in a genuine or original way
items.example: The dish is cooked authentically, with no shortcuts.
items.exampleCN: 这道菜做得地道，没有偷工减料。

items.meaning: to establish the genuineness of something
items.example: The signature was authenticated by a handwriting expert.
items.exampleCN: 签名经笔迹专家鉴定为真。

items.example: Authentication of the painting took six weeks.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画的鉴定用了六周。

items.meaning: one who or that which verifies
items.example: The token works as a second authenticator.
items.exampleCN: 这个令牌充当第二重认证器。

items.example: The label warned buyers of inauthentic goods.
items.exampleCN: 标签提醒买家提防仿冒商品。

items.meaning: the quality of being false or staged
items.example: Critics noted the inauthenticity of the accent.
items.exampleCN: 评论者指出那口音不自然。

items.example: The word authenticness was current in the 1620s.
items.exampleCN: authenticness 一词在 17 世纪 20 年代通用。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 真正的；原初的；有权威的

latinEntries.structure: auctor (noun; not the source of authentic)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 创始者；作者（并非 authentic 的来源）

definition_zh: 鉴定（真伪）；证明……真实；验证身份；（计算机）认证
definition_en: to prove that something is genuine or that a person or device is what it claims to be
core_image: 一枚旧印章在放大镜下被逐条比对纹路
scene: 拍卖行的人把画翻到背面，对着灯看纸的年轮。An expert was called in to authenticate the painting.
sceneCN: 这里指鉴定物件是否为真品（第 1 个义项：证明某物为真）；句意为请来专家鉴定这幅画的真伪。

pos.zh: 鉴定真伪；证明真实性；验证身份；认证

senses.title: To prove something genuine
senses.definition: to establish that an object or document is what it claims to be
senses.definitionCN: 确认某物或文件确如其声称
senses.example: An expert was called in to authenticate the painting.
senses.exampleCN: 请来一位专家鉴定这幅画。
senses.why: Greek authentikos meant genuine or original, and the verb makes that judgement an act.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 authentikos 意为「真的、原本的」，动词把这个判断变成一项行为。

senses.title: To verify a person's identity
senses.definition: to confirm that a person is who they say they are
senses.definitionCN: 确认某人确为其自称之人
senses.example: The bank authenticates every caller before moving money.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在动钱之前会验证每一位来电者。
senses.why: Identity is the modern field where the word is used most often.
senses.whyCN: 身份是现代使用这个词最频繁的领域。

senses.title: To certify a signature or seal
senses.definition: to confirm that a signature or seal was made by the right hand
senses.definitionCN: 确认签名或印章出自有权之人
senses.example: A notary authenticated the signature on the deed.
senses.exampleCN: 公证人证明了契据上的签名。
senses.why: Law needs a trusted hand to say that another hand was genuine.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一双可信的手来宣告另一双手为真。

senses.title: To log a user into a system
senses.titleCN: 计算机系统中认证用户
senses.definition: to check credentials before granting access
senses.definitionCN: 在授予访问权之前核验凭证
senses.example: The app authenticates users with a one-time code.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用用一次性验证码认证用户。
senses.why: Computing shortened the legal judgement into a routine check.
senses.whyCN: 计算技术把法律的判断压缩成例行核验。

senses.title: To establish evidence as genuine
senses.definition: to show that evidence is original and unaltered
senses.definitionCN: 证明证据为原件且未被改动
senses.example: The court must authenticate the recording before using it.
senses.exampleCN: 法院在使用录音之前必须先确认其为真。
senses.why: Evidence must be traced to its source before it can speak.
senses.whyCN: 证据必须先追溯到来源，才能开口作证。

senses.title: To verify a financial transaction
senses.definition: to confirm that a payment or message came from the stated sender
senses.definitionCN: 确认支付或讯息确由所称发送者发出
senses.example: The network authenticates the transfer in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 网络在几秒内核验了这笔转账。
senses.why: Money moves only when the sender can be proven.
senses.whyCN: 只有发送者能被证明，钱才动得了。

senses.title: To judge a work of art
senses.definition: to decide whether a work was made by the claimed artist or period
senses.definitionCN: 判定作品是否出自所称的艺术家或年代
senses.example: Two laboratories authenticated the canvas.
senses.exampleCN: 两家实验室鉴定了这幅画布。
senses.why: The art market rests on a judgement that a hand and a date are real.
senses.whyCN: 艺术市场靠的是一个判断：那双手与那个年代是真的。

senses.title: To establish a claim as credible
senses.definition: to give a statement enough support to be believed
senses.definitionCN: 给某说法足够支撑，使其可信
senses.example: The data authenticate his account of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 数据证实了他对事故的叙述。
senses.why: The word can widen from objects to any claim that needs a warrant.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以从物件扩展到任何需要凭据的说法。

intro.en: Authenticate comes from Greek authentikos, genuine or original, through Latin authenticus and French authentique, with the English verb suffix -ate. The direct source is clear; the second element of the Greek noun authentes is source uncertain.
intro.cn: authenticate 源自希腊 authentikos「真的、原本的」，经拉丁 authenticus 与法语 authentique，再加英语动词后缀 -ate。直接来源清楚；希腊名词 authentes 的第二成分来源不确定。

items.en: Autos meant self, and it is the first element of authentes.
items.cn: autos 意为自身，是 authentes 的第一成分。

items.en: Authentes meant one who acts on his own authority, a master or doer; the second element is often read as a doer but is source uncertain.
items.cn: authentes 意为凭自身权威行事的人，即主人或行为者；第二成分常被解作「做者」，但来源不确定。

items.en: Authentikos meant genuine, original and principal, said of things that carry their own authority.
items.cn: authentikos 意为真的、原本的、主要的，用于本身带有权威的事物。

items.en: Latin authenticus and French authentique carried the adjective into English.
items.cn: 拉丁 authenticus 与法语 authentique 把这个形容词带进英语。

items.en: English added the verb suffix -ate, making the judgement an action.
items.cn: 英语加上动词后缀 -ate，把判断变成动作。

items.en: Computing gave the verb its busiest modern home, where credentials replace seals.
items.cn: 计算技术给了这个动词最繁忙的现代归宿，凭证取代了印章。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek genuine-stem; the second group names checking and proving.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语「真」的词干；第二组是核验与证明的近义说法。

entries.definition: Genuine and true to its claimed origin.
entries.definitionCN: 真正的，符合其声称来源的。

entries.definition: The quality of being genuine.
entries.definitionCN: 真实性。

entries.definition: The act or process of proving genuineness.
entries.definitionCN: 证明真实性的行为或过程。

entries.definition: A person or device that verifies identity.
entries.definitionCN: 验证身份的人或装置。

entries.definition: A writer or originator; from Latin auctor, not from Greek authentes.
entries.definitionCN: 作者或创始者；出自拉丁 auctor，与希腊 authentes 无关。

entries.definition: To check that something is true or accurate.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事物为真或准确。

entries.definition: To confirm that something is valid or acceptable.
entries.definitionCN: 确认某事物有效或可接受。

entries.definition: To state officially that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 正式声明某事物为真。

entries.definition: To establish the truth of something more firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 更牢固地确立某事物的真实性。

entries.definition: To bear witness to a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 为某一事实作证。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek source, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊来源、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Autos is self, and authentes is one who acts on his own authority.
normal.cn: autos 是自身，authentes 是凭自身权威行事的人。

normal.en: Authentic is the adjective, authenticity the noun, authentication the process.
normal.cn: authentic 是形容词，authenticity 是名词，authentication 是过程。

normal.en: A notary authenticates a signature; a server authenticates a user.
normal.cn: 公证人证明签名，服务器认证用户。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: authenticate a painting, authenticate a document, authenticate a transaction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：鉴定画作、证明文件、核验交易。

normal.en: Author looks close but comes from a different Latin word.
normal.cn: author 形近，却出自另一个拉丁词。

abstract.en: Authenticate is a lens over an old seal, line by line until the pattern matches.
abstract.cn: 鉴定是拿放大镜对着一枚旧印章，一条条纹路比对到吻合。

abstract.en: A thing is authentic when its origin can be traced, not merely when it looks right.
abstract.cn: 事物之为真，在于来源可追，而不只在于看起来像。

abstract.en: Every password is a small claim that someone must prove.
abstract.cn: 每一个密码都是一个待证明的小小声称。

examples.en: The dealer refused to authenticate the letter without its envelope.
examples.cn: 没有信封，经销商拒绝证明这封信为真。

examples.en: The system authenticates each device before it joins the network.
examples.cn: 设备加入网络之前，系统会逐一认证。

examples.en: No one could authenticate the story of the missing hours.
examples.cn: 没有人能证实那几小时空白里的说法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥森提凯特」——把真东西挑出来盖章：鉴定为真

root: 希腊 authentikos「真的、原本的、主要的」← authentes「凭自身权威行事者」← autos「自身」加一个来源不确定的第二成分；经拉丁 authenticus 与法语 authentique 进入英语，再加动词后缀 -ate。同族 authentic、authenticity、authentication；author 形近但出自拉丁 auctor，与此无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses prove genuineness in objects, persons, seals, systems, evidence, payments, art and claims.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在物件、人、印章、系统、证据、支付、艺术品与说法上证明真实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old seal under a lens, its lines matched one by one.
core.cn: 核心意象：放大镜下的旧印章，纹路被逐条比对。

branches.en: THE GENUINE OBJECT: a painting or document traced to its true origin.
branches.cn: 真品：被追溯到真实来源的画作或文件。

branches.en: THE PROVEN PERSON: a caller or user confirmed as themselves.
branches.cn: 被证明的人：被确认确为其本人的来电者或用户。

branches.en: THE TRUSTED MARK AND THE EVIDENCE: a certified signature and a recording traced to its source.
branches.cn: 可信的印记与证据：被证明的签名与被追溯来源的录音。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM CHECK: credentials accepted and a payment confirmed from its sender.
branches.cn: 系统核验：凭证被接受，支付被确认由发送者发出。

branches.en: THE CREDIBLE CLAIM: a story given enough support to be believed.
branches.cn: 可信的说法：获得足够支撑而可被相信的叙述。

intro.en: Authenticate is the Greek genuine-adjective plus the English verb suffix -ate; the Greek noun behind it has one uncertain element.
intro.cn: authenticate 是希腊语「真」的形容词加英语动词后缀 -ate；其背后的希腊名词有一个成分不确定。

latinIntro.en: Greek authentikos reached Latin as authenticus and then French; the Latin forms are carriers, not the origin.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 authentikos 以 authenticus 进入拉丁，再进法语；拉丁形式是载体，不是源头。

items.example: The first element points at a thing acting on its own.
items.exampleCN: 第一成分指向凭自身行动之物。

items.meaning: one acting on his own authority
items.example: The noun joins self to a doer of uncertain form.
items.exampleCN: 名词把「自身」与一个形式不确定的「做者」相加。

items.example: The adjective turns authority into genuineness.
items.exampleCN: 形容词把权威变成真实性。

items.example: Latin carried the Greek adjective westward.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个希腊形容词向西传递。

items.example: French brought the word to English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个词带到英语。

items.example: The adjective survives beside the longer verb.
items.exampleCN: 形容词与更长的动词并存。

items.example: The suffix turns the quality into an act.
The noun names the process rather than the quality.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名过程，而非性质。

items.example: The noun belongs to the adjective, not the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词属于形容词，而非动词。

items.example: It also builds validate, activate and calculate.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 validate、activate 与 calculate。

definition_zh: 授权；批准；准许（英式拼写）
definition_en: to give official permission for something, or to give someone the power to do something; the British spelling of authorize
core_image: 一枚公章落下，某件事从此被准许去做
scene: 财务主管在付款单上签字，允许这笔钱汇出。Only the director can authorise a payment of this size.
sceneCN: 这里 authorise 是「批准、准许」（第 1 个义项）；句意是只有主管能批准这么大额的付款。

pos.zh: 及物动词：授权；批准（英式拼写）

derivatives.zh: 加否定前缀：未经授权的

senses.title: To give official permission
senses.definition: to give formal permission for an action, payment or release
senses.definitionCN: 正式准许某项行动、付款或发布
senses.example: The board met to authorise the extra spending.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会开会批准额外开支。
senses.why: The root auctor meant an originator who carries weight, so to authorise is to let that weight stand behind an act.
senses.whyCN: 词根 auctor 指有分量的开创者，所以批准就是让那份分量站到某件事背后。

senses.title: To empower a person to act
senses.definition: to give a person the official power to do something on behalf of another
senses.definitionCN: 正式赋予某人代表他人行事的权力
senses.example: We authorise agents to sign for us.
senses.exampleCN: 我们授权代理人代我们签字。
senses.why: Permission can attach to a thing or to a person; here the weight is transferred into someone else's hands.
senses.whyCN: 许可既可给事也可给人；这里把分量交到别人手里。

senses.title: To clear a payment or transaction
senses.definition: to approve a financial transaction so that it can proceed
senses.definitionCN: 核准一笔金融交易，使其得以进行
senses.example: The bank must authorise the transfer first.
senses.exampleCN: 银行必须先核准这笔转账。
senses.why: Modern banking kept the old sense of official sanction, now applied to money moving between accounts.
senses.whyCN: 现代银行业保留了「正式许可」的旧义，如今用在账户间流动的钱上。

senses.title: To allow access or use
senses.definition: to grant someone the right to enter a system or use a resource
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人进入系统或使用资源的权利
senses.example: Only staff are authorised to use this door.
senses.exampleCN: 只有员工获准使用这扇门。
senses.why: The stamp of permission becomes a key: being authorised means the gate will open for you.
senses.whyCN: 许可的公章变成一把钥匙：获准就意味着门会为你打开。

senses.title: To sanction force or a measure
senses.definition: to give official approval for the use of force or a strong measure
senses.definitionCN: 正式批准动用武力或采取强硬措施
senses.example: Parliament voted to authorise the deployment.
senses.exampleCN: 议会投票批准这次部署。
senses.why: The gravest use of the word is when a whole institution lends its weight to an act of force.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最重的用法，是整个机构把分量借给一次武力行动。

senses.title: To make a document official
senses.definition: to approve a text or version so that it becomes the official one
senses.definitionCN: 认可某文本或版本，使其成为正式版本
senses.example: The society authorised a new edition of the rules.
senses.exampleCN: 学会批准了规则的新版本。
senses.why: Here permission fixes what counts as the real version, echoing the older sense of authentic.
senses.whyCN: 这里的许可确定了什么才算正式版本，呼应「真迹、正式」的旧义。

intro.en: Authorise is the British spelling of a verb built on authority: to lend the weight of an originator to an act.
intro.cn: authorise 是一个建立在「权力」之上的动词的英式拼写：把开创者的分量借给某件事。

items.en: Augere meant to increase or make grow; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: augere 意为「增加、使生长」；更深的原始印欧语词根属于重构形式，并无文字记录。

items.en: Auctor named the one who makes something grow or begin: an originator, later a writer or a seller.
items.cn: auctor 指使事物生长或开始的人：开创者，后来也指作者或卖方。

items.en: Auctoritas meant influence and the weight of a judgment, the noun behind authority.
items.cn: auctoritas 意为影响力与判断的分量，是「权力」一词背后的名词。

items.en: The verb auctorizare meant to give authority to, to sanction or confirm.
items.cn: 动词 auctorizare 意为「赋予权力、批准、确认」。

items.en: Old French autoriser carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 autoriser 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语。

items.en: British English settled on the -ise ending, while American English kept -ize; both spellings are the same word.
items.cn: 英式英语定型为 -ise 词尾，美式英语保留 -ize；两种拼写是同一个词。

note.en: The look-alike group is the authority family plus the American spelling; the near-meaning group grades ways of giving permission.
note.cn: 形近组是「权力」词族加美式拼写；近义组按给予许可的方式分级。

entries.definition: the same verb in American spelling
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的美式拼写，意思完全相同。

entries.definition: the power or the body that holds it
entries.definitionCN: 权力；当局；同族名词。

entries.definition: official permission, British spelling
entries.definitionCN: 授权；批准，英式名词。

entries.definition: a writer or originator
entries.definitionCN: 作者；开创者，同族。

entries.definition: to allow something, often by a rule
entries.definitionCN: 允许；常指规则上的放行，分量较轻。

entries.definition: to accept as satisfactory or agree to
entries.definitionCN: 批准；认可，侧重同意而非赋权。

entries.definition: to give official approval, or a penalty
entries.definitionCN: 批准；制裁，正式用语，另有反义。

entries.definition: to give someone the power or confidence to act
entries.definitionCN: 赋权；给予权力或信心，较抽象。

normalIntro.en: Authorise is authority turned into a verb with -ise: to let an act carry official weight.
normalIntro.cn: authorise 就是把「权力」加 -ise 变成动词：让某件事带上正式的分量。

normal.en: The stem is the same as in author and authority.
normal.cn: 词干与作者、权力两词相同。

normal.en: British English writes -ise, American writes -ize.
normal.cn: 英式写 -ise，美式写 -ize。

normal.en: The noun is authorisation, also with -ise.
normal.cn: 名词是授权，同样用 -ise。

normal.en: Be authorised to do means have permission to do.
normal.cn: 获准做某事就是有许可去做。

normal.en: Unauthorised adds the negative prefix un-.
normal.cn: 未经授权加否定前缀 un-。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp falling onto a payment slip.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚公章落在付款单上。

abstract.en: Picture a key handed to an agent.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙交到代理人手里。

abstract.en: Picture a gate opening only for the approved.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门只为获准者打开。

examples.en: Only the director can authorise a refund.
examples.cn: 只有主管能批准退款。

examples.en: The council authorised the new building plan.
examples.cn: 市政会批准了新的建筑方案。

examples.en: She is not authorised to speak to the press.
examples.cn: 她未获授权向媒体发言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：author「开创者」加 -ise「使……」——让开创者的分量落到某件事上，就是批准、授权；英式拼 -ise。

root: 拉丁语 augere「使生长」派生 auctor「开创者」与 auctoritas「分量、权力」，中世纪拉丁语 auctorizare「赋予权力」经古法语 autoriser 进入英语；英式拼作 -ise，美式拼作 -ize。

sensesIntro.en: One idea, lending official weight, spreads to permitting an act, empowering a person, clearing money, granting access, sanctioning force and fixing a text.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个核心「借出正式分量」展开为准许某事、授权某人、核准钱款、给予访问、批准武力与确定文本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an official stamp falling so that an act is allowed to proceed
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚公章落下，某件事从此被准许去做

branches.en: a board permitting extra spending
an agent empowered to sign
a bank clearing a transfer
a gate opened, or force sanctioned
an edition made official

intro.en: The verb ending -ise turns the authority stem into an action; the same stem builds the noun and the adjective.
intro.cn: 动词词尾 -ise 把「权力」词干变成动作；同一词干还造出名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin auctorizare, to give authority, comes from auctoritas and auctor, from augere, to increase.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 auctorizare「赋予权力」来自 auctoritas 与 auctor，再来自 augere「增加」。

items.meaning: power or the body holding it

latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个动词是深层词根。
这个名词产生「作者」。
这个名词产生「权力」。
这个动词是动词来源。

definition_zh: 有权威的；可靠的；官方认定的；带命令口吻的；权威性的（定本、裁定）
definition_en: carrying weight because of recognised expertise or official standing, and sometimes describing a commanding manner
core_image: 档案馆阅览室里，编者把初版校样与手稿逐行对照，在页边写下勘定
scene: 档案馆阅览室里，一位编者把初版校样与手稿逐行对照，在页边写下勘定。The authoritative edition corrected errors that had stood for a century.
sceneCN: 这里指「权威性的定本」，对应第 4 个义项：经严格考订、被公认为标准版本的著作；句意为这个权威定本改正了沿用百年的错误。画面要点：阅览室长桌、校样、页边批注。

pos.zh: 有权威的；可信的（因专业或地位而具分量）
官方的；经正式认定的
带命令口吻的；不容置疑的

collocations.phrase: the authoritative work on the subject

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

derivatives.zh: 以权威方式；带权威口吻地

senses.title: Reliable because of expertise
senses.definition: describing information or a person whose judgement carries weight because of deep knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 形容因知识深厚而具有分量的信息或人物
senses.example: She is authoritative on the history of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这个地区的历史研究上很有权威。
senses.why: the Latin noun behind the word meant influence or prestige, so authority first means standing, and authoritative means having that standing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁名词意为影响力与声望，所以 authority 首先指分量，而 authoritative 指具有这种分量的。

senses.title: Officially recognised
senses.definition: describing a text, list or statement issued by a body with the right to settle the matter
senses.definitionCN: 形容由有权定夺此事的机构发布的文本、名册或声明
senses.example: The registry is the authoritative list of licensed doctors.
senses.exampleCN: 这份登记册是持证医师的权威名册。
senses.why: recognition can come from office as well as from knowledge, and the word covers both sources of weight.
senses.whyCN: 分量既可来自学问，也可来自职位，这个词同时涵盖这两种来源。

senses.title: A commanding manner
senses.definition: describing a tone or gesture that expects to be obeyed rather than discussed
senses.definitionCN: 形容期待被服从、而非被讨论的语气或姿态
senses.example: He answered in the authoritative tone of a headmaster.
senses.exampleCN: 他用校长那种不容置疑的口气回答。
senses.why: a person with weight can speak as if the question were closed, and the adjective then describes the manner rather than the knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 有分量的人说话时可以像是问题已经定了，此时这个形容词描述的是态度，而非学识。

senses.title: The standard edition or reference work
senses.titleCN: 标准定本或权威工具书
senses.definition: describing a book that others cite because it has settled the text or the facts
senses.definitionCN: 形容因已厘定文本或事实而被他人引用的著作
senses.example: The authoritative edition corrected errors that had stood for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这个权威定本改正了沿用百年的错误。
senses.why: a work becomes a standard when the field stops checking it and starts citing it, and the adjective marks that point.
senses.whyCN: 当同行不再核查、转而引用一部著作时，它就成了标准，这个形容词标记的正是那一刻。

senses.title: A binding ruling
senses.definition: describing a decision by a court or regulator that others must follow
senses.definitionCN: 形容法院或监管机构作出、他人必须遵从的决定
senses.example: Only an authoritative ruling can settle the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 只有权威裁定才能了结这场争端。
senses.why: when a body can compel, its word has weight in the strongest sense, and the adjective attaches to the decision.
senses.whyCN: 当某机构能强制执行时，它的话就有最强意义上的分量，这个形容词便附着在决定上。

senses.title: The definitive account
senses.definition: describing a study or report that others treat as the fullest and best-supported version
senses.definitionCN: 形容被同行视为最完整、证据最充分的著作或报告
senses.example: Her book remains the authoritative account of the negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 她那本书仍是关于这些谈判的权威叙述。
senses.why: an account that ends argument is authoritative in the same way a standard edition is, by consent of the field.
senses.whyCN: 一部结束争论的叙述，与标准定本一样是靠同行的认可而具权威的。

senses.title: A recognised figure in a field
senses.titleCN: 某一领域公认的代表人物
senses.definition: describing a scholar or official whom others defer to on a particular question
senses.definitionCN: 形容在某一问题上被他人请教的学者或官员
senses.example: He became the authoritative voice on water law.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了水法问题上的权威声音。
senses.why: weight attaches to persons as well as to texts, and one sentence can mark both the expertise and the deference.
senses.whyCN: 分量既附在文本上，也附在人身上，一句话就能同时标出专业与被请教这两件事。

senses.title: Abstract: weight that needs no argument
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：不必论证即有分量
senses.definition: in general use, describing something accepted without challenge because of who produced it
senses.definitionCN: 泛指因出自某人之手而被直接接受、不再追问的东西
senses.example: The memo carried an authoritative silence on the cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这份备忘录对成本问题保持一种权威式的沉默。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the effect, namely that the question is treated as closed.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只留下效果，即那个问题被当作已经定了。

intro.en: Authoritative rests on the Latin noun for authority, which grew from a verb meaning to increase, and on an English adjective ending. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: authoritative 立在一个意为「权威」的拉丁名词与一个英语形容词词尾上，而那个拉丁名词又出自一个意为「增加」的动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Augere meant 'to increase, make grow'; the Indo-European root behind it is reconstructed rather than attested, so any earlier form cited is a reconstruction.
items.cn: augere 意为「增加、使生长」；它背后的印欧语词根属重构而非有书证的形式，因此凡为其引出的更早形式都是重构形式。

items.en: Auctor named the one who causes something to grow or begin: an originator, a promoter, later a seller and a writer.
items.cn: auctor 指使事物生长或开始的那一位：创始者、推动者，后来也指卖方与作者。

items.en: Auctoritas meant influence, prestige and the weight of a judgement, and it belonged to the senate as much as to a single writer.
items.cn: auctoritas 意为影响力、声望与判断的分量，它既属于元老院，也属于单个作者。

items.en: Old French autorite carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century as authority, first as a personal quality and later as an office or a body.
items.cn: 古法语 autorite 在十四世纪把这个名词以 authority 的形式带入英语，最初指个人品质，后指职位或机构。

items.en: Authoritative was formed on authority with the ending -ative and first meant 'having power to command belief', before it also came to describe a commanding manner.
items.cn: authoritative 由 authority 加表示「具有……性质」的形容词词尾构成，最初意为「具有令人信服之力」，后来也用来形容命令式的态度。

note.en: Group one holds words from the authority family that are easily confused with this adjective; group two holds adjectives of reliability and command.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 authority 词族、容易与本词混淆的词；第二组是表示可靠或命令意味的形容词。

entries.definition: Describing a system that demands obedience and limits opposition; it is a charge against a regime, not a compliment about a source.
entries.definitionCN: 形容要求服从、限制反对的政治体制；它是对政权的指控，而非对信息来源的褒扬。

entries.definition: Describing someone or something given formal permission; a work can be authorised without being authoritative.
entries.definitionCN: 形容获得正式许可的人或物；一部作品可以是获准发行的，却未必具有权威性。

entries.definition: The person who wrote a work; authorship is a fact, while authoritative describes the standing the work has gained.
entries.definitionCN: 指作品的写作者；作者身份是事实，而 authoritative 描述作品获得的地位。

entries.definition: Meaning real or not counterfeit, as an authentic signature; a document can be authentic and still be wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 意为真实的、非伪造的，如真实签名；文件可以是真的，内容却可能是错的。

entries.definition: Describing the version that ends dispute, as a definitive study; authoritative adds who is recognised as having the right to settle it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容终结争论的版本，如定论性研究；authoritative 另添「谁被认可有权定夺」这层意思。

entries.definition: Describing something that can be depended on to be accurate; reliability is about error rates, not about prestige.
entries.definitionCN: 形容可以依赖其准确性的事物；可靠性关乎出错率，而非声望。

entries.definition: Describing what comes from a body with formal standing; an official statement may still be wrong or disputed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容来自具有正式地位之机构的事物；官方声明也可能是错的或有争议的。

entries.definition: Describing a manner or presence that expects obedience; it covers the third sense alone and says nothing about knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 形容期待被服从的态度或气场；它只涵盖第三义项，与学识无关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The base verb meant to make grow, so an author is one who makes something come into being, and authority is the weight that follows.
normal.cn: 基础动词意为「使生长」，所以作者是使某物出现的人，而权威是随之而来的分量。

normal.en: The family runs authority, author, authorize, authorization and authoritatively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括权威、作者、授权、授权文件与以权威方式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: an authoritative source, an authoritative account, an authoritative ruling.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：权威来源、权威记述、权威裁定。

normal.en: The word can praise a source and also describe a bossy tone, so context decides the colour.
normal.cn: 这个词既能称赞信息来源，也能形容专断口气，语气由语境决定。

normal.en: The trap to avoid is authoritarian, which describes a regime rather than a reference book.
normal.cn: 要避开的陷阱是 authoritarian，那词描述政权，而非参考书。

abstract.en: Picture a book so heavily cited that nobody bothers to check it again.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书被引用得太多，以至于没人再去核对它。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand that ends a discussion without a vote.
abstract.cn: 想象一只举起的手，不用表决就结束了讨论。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp on a page that makes every later objection look unnecessary.
abstract.cn: 想象纸页上的一枚印章，让之后所有异议都显得多余。

examples.en: The committee waited for an authoritative ruling on the boundary.
examples.cn: 委员会等待关于边界的权威裁定。

examples.en: His account of the war is still treated as authoritative.
examples.cn: 他对那场战争的叙述仍被视为权威。

examples.en: She spoke in a tone that was almost too authoritative.
examples.cn: 她说话的口吻几乎过于命令式了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「权威 + 形容词」——一开口就让人不必再追问的那份分量 → 有权威的

root: authoritative 由 authority 加形容词词尾构成；authority 经古法语出自拉丁 auctoritas「影响力、声望」，源头 auctor「创始者、作者」，再上溯到 augere「使生长」。印欧语词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one weight: knowledge earns it, office confirms it, a manner displays it, a standard edition embodies it, a ruling enforces it, a definitive account earns it by consent, a person carries it, and finally anything accepted without argument has it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一份分量展开：学问赢得它，职位确认它，态度展示它，标准定本体现它，裁定强制执行它，定论性叙述靠同行认可得到它，个人承载它，最后任何被直接接受、不再追问的东西都具有它。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a collated proof with marginal corrections, cited by everyone afterwards.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份逐行校勘、写满页边批注的校样，此后被所有人引用。

branches.en: EXPERTISE: deep knowledge is the first source of the weight the word describes.
branches.cn: 专业：深厚的知识是这个词所描述之分量的第一个来源。

branches.en: OFFICE: a body with the right to settle a matter gives the same weight through a list or a ruling.
branches.cn: 职位：有权定夺某事的机构，通过一份名册或一项裁定给出同样的分量。

branches.en: MANNER: weight can be heard in a tone that treats the question as closed.
branches.cn: 态度：分量可以从语气里听出来，那种语气把问题当作已经定了。

branches.en: CANON: a standard edition and a definitive account are both settled by the consent of the field.
branches.cn: 定本：标准版本与定论性叙述，都是靠同行的认可而定下来的。

branches.en: PERSON AND EFFECT: one figure can carry the weight, and in the end the only test is that nobody asks again.
branches.cn: 人与效果：一个人可以承载这份分量，而最终的检验就是没人再追问。

intro.en: Authoritative is a noun of standing plus an adjective ending, and the noun in turn rests on a Latin verb of growth.
intro.cn: authoritative 是一个表示分量的名词加形容词词尾，而那个名词又立在一个意为「生长」的拉丁动词上。

latinIntro.en: Latin auctor and auctoritas supply author, authority and authorize, all from the idea of causing something to begin or grow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 auctor 与 auctoritas 衍生出作者、权威与授权，全都出自「使某物开始或生长」这一想法。

items.example: The verb supplies the idea of causing growth.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「促成生长」的意思。

items.example: The originator is the one who makes a thing begin.
items.exampleCN: 创始者就是使一件事开始的人。

items.example: The noun named weight rather than legal power.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指分量，而非法律权力。

items.structure: Old French autorite, from Latin auctoritas
items.example: The word moved from prestige to office.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从声望转指职位。

items.example: The ending turns the noun of standing into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把表示分量的名词变成形容词。

items.example: The writer is literally the one who causes the work.
items.exampleCN: 作者字面上就是使作品出现的人。
工作在未获书面许可的情况下开始了。

items.example: The label criticises a regime, not a reference book.
items.exampleCN: 这个标签批评的是政权，而非参考书。

definition_zh: 权力，职权；权限；当局，官方机构；授权；权威，专家；权威著作；权威性；消息来源
definition_en: the power to give orders, an official body that has such power, a person whose knowledge is trusted, or the quality of being reliable
core_image: 一枚印章压在文件上，纸面立刻有了分量
scene: 小区要修路，居民先去找能拍板的那一方。The local authority approved the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 authority 是「当局、官方机构」（第 3 个义项）；句意是地方当局批准了这项计划。

pos.zh: 名词：权力；当局；权威

senses.title: Power to give orders
senses.definition: the right or power to give orders, make decisions and expect obedience
senses.definitionCN: 下命令、作决定并要求他人服从的资格或力量
senses.example: The manager has the authority to hire staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理有权雇用员工。
senses.why: Latin auctor meant an originator, and the noun named the weight an originator carries, so this power comes from standing rather than force.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 auctor 意为开创者，派生名词指开创者身上的分量，所以这种权力来自地位而非武力。

senses.title: The limits of that power
senses.definition: the range of matters in which a person or body is allowed to act
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某机构获准处理事务的范围
senses.example: Signing that contract is outside my authority.
senses.exampleCN: 签那份合同超出了我的权限。
senses.why: Once power is granted it has edges, so the same word turns from the power itself to the fence drawn around it.
senses.whyCN: 权力一旦被赋予就有了边界，于是同一个词从「权力本身」转指「权力周围的那道栅栏」。

senses.title: An official body
senses.definition: an organization or government department that holds public power, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 掌握公共权力的组织或政府部门，常用复数形式
senses.example: The local authority approved the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 地方当局批准了这项计划。
senses.why: Power moves from a person to an institution, so the plural came to mean the people who run a city or a public service.
senses.whyCN: 权力从个人转到机构身上，于是复数形式常指管理一座城市或某项公共事务的部门。

senses.title: Permission granted
senses.definition: official permission for an action, or the document that gives such permission
senses.definitionCN: 对某项行动的正式许可，或给出这种许可的文件
senses.example: The work began on the authority of a signed letter.
senses.exampleCN: 工程凭一封签字信件获得授权后开工。
senses.why: The power to allow becomes the allowance itself, which is why the phrase with of means with permission from someone.
senses.whyCN: 「准许的权力」变成了「准许本身」，所以带 of 的那个短语就是「凭某人的许可」。

senses.title: A trusted expert
senses.definition: a person whose knowledge or judgment is respected in a particular field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域知识或判断受人尊重的人
senses.example: She is an authority on ancient coins.
senses.exampleCN: 她是古钱币方面的权威。
senses.why: Here the weight is intellectual rather than official: the person is trusted for learning, not for holding an office.
senses.whyCN: 这里的分量是学问上的而非官职上的：此人受信任靠的是学识，而不是职位。

senses.title: A standard reference work
senses.definition: a book or source accepted as the reliable statement of a subject
senses.definitionCN: 被公认为某学科可靠说法的书籍或资料
senses.example: That grammar remains the authority on the old dialect.
senses.exampleCN: 那本语法书仍是这种古老方言的权威依据。
senses.why: If a person can carry weight, so can a text, and the word slides from the expert to the work the expert wrote.
senses.whyCN: 既然人能有分量，文本也能有分量，于是这个词从专家滑向专家写出的著作。

senses.title: Convincing weight
senses.titleCN: 权威性；令人信服的分量
senses.definition: the quality of being reliable and of commanding belief
senses.definitionCN: 可靠、令人信服并使人愿意接受的性质
senses.example: She spoke with quiet authority.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话平静却很有分量。
senses.why: Stripped of offices and of persons, the word names the abstract quality that makes a statement hard to doubt.
senses.whyCN: 去掉官职与具体的人之后，这个词指那种让人难以怀疑的抽象性质。

senses.title: A source of information
senses.definition: the source on which a statement is believed, as in the phrase on good authority
senses.definitionCN: 使人相信某个说法的来源，如「据可靠消息」这一说法
senses.example: I have it on good authority that the date will change.
senses.exampleCN: 据可靠消息，日期会有变动。
senses.why: The trusted person becomes the reason for believing, so the phrase names where news comes from rather than who commands.
senses.whyCN: 受信任的人变成了相信的理由，于是这个短语指的是消息从何而来，而不是谁在下命令。

intro.en: Authority names the weight that an originator carries.
intro.cn: authority 指开创者身上所带的分量。

items.en: Augere meant to increase or make grow; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: augere 意为「增加、使生长」；更深的原始印欧语词根属于重构形式，并无文字记录。

items.en: Auctor named the one who makes something grow or begin: an originator, a promoter, later a writer or a seller.
items.cn: auctor 指使事物生长或开始的人：开创者、推动者，后来也指作者或卖方。

items.en: Auctoritas meant influence, prestige and the weight of a judgment, and it belonged to the senate as much as to one person.
items.cn: auctoritas 意为影响力、威望与判断的分量，既属于个人，也属于元老院这样的机构。

items.en: Old French autorite carried the noun across, keeping the sense of rightful power.
items.cn: 古法语 autorite 把这个名词带过来，保留「正当权力」的意思。

items.en: English authority covered personal weight, official power and expert opinion at the same time.
items.cn: 中古英语的 authority 同时涵盖个人分量、官方权力与专家意见。

items.en: The plural became the normal word for official bodies, while the phrase on good authority fixed the sense of a trusted source.
items.cn: 复数形式成为指官方机构的常用说法，而「据可靠消息」这一短语则固定了「可靠来源」这一义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the auctor root; the near-meaning group gives words for power and expertise.
note.cn: 形近组共享 auctor 词根；近义组是表示权力与专业知识的词。

entries.definition: a writer or originator
entries.definitionCN: 作者；发起者

entries.definition: to give official permission
entries.definitionCN: 授权

entries.definition: commanding and reliable
entries.definitionCN: 权威的

entries.definition: official permission given by someone in power
entries.definitionCN: 授权；批准，由掌权者给出的正式许可。

entries.definition: the ability to control others
entries.definitionCN: 权力

entries.definition: the act of directing something
entries.definitionCN: 控制

entries.definition: a person with deep knowledge
entries.definitionCN: 专家

entries.definition: the official range of power to make legal decisions
entries.definitionCN: 管辖权；司法权限，强调范围而不是分量。

normalIntro.en: Authority is weight: official weight, institutional weight, or the weight of knowledge.
normalIntro.cn: authority 是一种分量：官职的分量、机构的分量，或知识的分量。

normal.en: The root is the same as in author: an originator carries weight.
normal.cn: 词根与 author 相同：开创者身上带着分量。

normal.en: The plural authorities usually means official bodies, not several powers.
normal.cn: 复数 authorities 通常指官方机构，而不是几种权力。

normal.en: An authority on a subject is a trusted expert.
normal.cn: an authority on a subject 指某领域可信的专家。

normal.en: The adjective authoritative keeps the -ative ending.
normal.cn: 形容词 authoritative 保留了 -ative 词尾。

normal.en: Do not confuse authority with author; one is weight, the other is a person.
normal.cn: 不要把 authority 与 author 混淆：一个是分量，一个是人。

abstract.en: See a stamp pressed onto a sheet of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章压在一张纸上。

abstract.en: See a raised hand that stops a whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起，整个房间都停下来。

abstract.en: See a thick reference book with a ribbon in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚厚的工具书，里面夹着书签带。

examples.en: The manager has the authority to hire staff.
examples.cn: 这位经理有权雇用员工。

examples.en: The local authority approved the plan.
examples.cn: 地方当局批准了这项计划。

examples.en: She is an authority on ancient coins.
examples.cn: 她是古钱币方面的权威。

dict_mnemonic.text: author（开创者）加 -ity：开创者说的话有分量，这分量就是权力；一群掌权的机构是当局；学问深到说话有分量的人就是权威。

root: 源自拉丁语 auctoritas「影响力、号令」，来自 auctor「开创者」，词根 augere 意为「使生长」；经古法语 autorite 进入英语，由「开创者的分量」引申为权力、官方机构与专业权威。

sensesIntro.en: One core idea, weight, spreads into the right to command, its limits, the body that holds it, the permission it gives, the expert, the standard book, the quality and the source.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个核心意象「分量」展开为下令的资格、它的边界、掌权的机构、给出的许可、专家、标准著作、性质与消息来源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an official stamp that makes a sheet of paper heavy.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚公章让一张纸变得有分量。

the local authority and the authorities
work begun on the authority of a letter
an expert and the standard book
quiet weight and a trusted source
branches.cn: 沉静的分量与可靠的来源

intro.en: The root auctor, 'originator', links authority with author and authorize.
intro.cn: 词根 auctor 意为「开创者」，把 authority 与 author、authorize 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin augere, 'to increase', is the deeper root of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 augere「增加」是整个词族更深的词源。

items.meaning: the power or the body that holds it
the state of being the author

latinEntries.example: Augere is the deep root of the family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 「使生长」是这个动词家族的深层词根。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 开创者；推动者；后来的作者
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个拉丁语名词产生了英语的「作者」。

latinEntries.example: Auctoritas was the weight of the senate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个词曾指元老院的分量。

definition_zh: 授权；批准；准许（美式拼写）
definition_en: to give official permission for something, or to give someone the power to do something; the American spelling of authorise
core_image: 一份许可文件签字生效，某件事被放行
scene: 系统弹出提示，需要管理员放行这次登录。An administrator must authorize each new device.
sceneCN: 这里 authorize 是「允许访问、放行」（第 4 个义项）；句意是每台新设备都必须由管理员放行。

pos.zh: 及物动词：授权；批准（美式拼写）

derivatives.zh: 加否定前缀：未经授权的

senses.title: To give official permission
senses.definition: to give formal permission for an action, payment or release
senses.definitionCN: 正式准许某项行动、付款或发布
senses.example: The committee voted to authorize the project.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会投票批准这个项目。
senses.why: The root auctor meant an originator who carries weight, so to authorize is to let that weight stand behind an act.
senses.whyCN: 词根 auctor 指有分量的开创者，所以批准就是让那份分量站到某件事背后。

senses.title: To empower a person to act
senses.definition: to give a person the official power to do something on behalf of another
senses.definitionCN: 正式赋予某人代表他人行事的权力
senses.example: The law authorizes officers to search the premises.
senses.exampleCN: 法律授权官员搜查这处房产。
senses.why: Permission can attach to a thing or to a person; here the weight is transferred into someone else's hands.
senses.whyCN: 许可既可给事也可给人；这里把分量交到别人手里。

senses.title: To clear a payment or transaction
senses.definition: to approve a financial transaction so that it can proceed
senses.definitionCN: 核准一笔金融交易，使其得以进行
senses.example: The card system authorizes the charge in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 刷卡系统几秒内就核准这笔扣款。
senses.why: Modern banking kept the old sense of official sanction, now applied to money moving between accounts.
senses.whyCN: 现代银行业保留了「正式许可」的旧义，如今用在账户间流动的钱上。

senses.title: To allow access or use
senses.definition: to grant someone the right to enter a system or use a resource
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人进入系统或使用资源的权利
senses.example: The software authorizes only registered users.
senses.exampleCN: 这款软件只放行注册用户。
senses.why: The stamp of permission becomes a key: being authorized means the gate will open for you.
senses.whyCN: 许可的公章变成一把钥匙：获准就意味着门会为你打开。

senses.title: To sanction force or a measure
senses.definition: to give official approval for the use of force or a strong measure
senses.definitionCN: 正式批准动用武力或采取强硬措施
senses.example: Congress moved to authorize the deployment.
senses.exampleCN: 国会着手批准这次部署。
senses.why: The gravest use of the word is when a whole institution lends its weight to an act of force.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最重的用法，是整个机构把分量借给一次武力行动。

senses.title: To make a version official
senses.definition: to approve a text, edition or account so that it becomes the official one
senses.definitionCN: 认可某文本、版本或记述，使其成为正式版本
senses.example: The family authorized a new biography.
senses.exampleCN: 家属授权了一部新传记。
senses.why: Here permission fixes what counts as the real version, echoing the older sense of authentic.
senses.whyCN: 这里的许可确定了什么才算正式版本，呼应「真迹、正式」的旧义。

intro.en: Authorize is the American spelling of a verb built on authority: to lend the weight of an originator to an act.
intro.cn: authorize 是一个建立在「权力」之上的动词的美式拼写：把开创者的分量借给某件事。

items.en: Augere meant to increase or make grow; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: augere 意为「增加、使生长」；更深的原始印欧语词根属于重构形式，并无文字记录。

items.en: Auctor named the one who makes something grow or begin: an originator, later a writer or a seller.
items.cn: auctor 指使事物生长或开始的人：开创者，后来也指作者或卖方。

items.en: Auctoritas meant influence and the weight of a judgment, the noun behind authority.
items.cn: auctoritas 意为影响力与判断的分量，是「权力」一词背后的名词。

items.en: The verb auctorizare meant to give authority to, to sanction or confirm.
items.cn: 动词 auctorizare 意为「赋予权力、批准、确认」。

items.en: Old French autoriser carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 autoriser 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语。

items.en: American English, following Noah Webster, preferred the -ize ending, while British English usually writes -ise.
items.cn: 美式英语追随韦伯斯特，偏好 -ize 词尾，而英式英语通常写 -ise。

note.en: The look-alike group is the authority family plus the British spelling; the near-meaning group grades ways of giving permission.
note.cn: 形近组是「权力」词族加英式拼写；近义组按给予许可的方式分级。

entries.definition: the same verb in British spelling
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的英式拼写，意思完全相同。

entries.definition: official permission, American spelling
entries.definitionCN: 授权；批准，美式名词。

entries.definition: the power or the body that holds it
entries.definitionCN: 权力；当局；同族名词。

entries.definition: a writer or originator
entries.definitionCN: 作者；开创者，同族。

entries.definition: to allow something, often by a rule
entries.definitionCN: 允许；常指规则上的放行，分量较轻。

entries.definition: to accept as satisfactory or agree to
entries.definitionCN: 批准；认可，侧重同意而非赋权。

entries.definition: to give official approval, or a penalty
entries.definitionCN: 批准；制裁，正式用语，另有反义。

entries.definition: to give someone the power or confidence to act
entries.definitionCN: 赋权；给予权力或信心，较抽象。

normalIntro.en: Authorize is authority turned into a verb with -ize: to let an act carry official weight.
normalIntro.cn: authorize 就是把「权力」加 -ize 变成动词：让某件事带上正式的分量。

normal.en: The stem is the same as in author and authority.
normal.cn: 词干与作者、权力两词相同。

normal.en: American English writes -ize, British writes -ise.
normal.cn: 美式写 -ize，英式写 -ise。

normal.en: The noun is authorization, also with -ize.
normal.cn: 名词是授权，同样用 -ize。

normal.en: Be authorized to do means have permission to do.
normal.cn: 获准做某事就是有许可去做。

normal.en: Unauthorized adds the negative prefix un-.
normal.cn: 未经授权加否定前缀 un-。

abstract.en: Picture a signature making a document take effect.
abstract.cn: 想象一个签名让文件生效。

abstract.en: Picture a login prompt waiting for an admin.
abstract.cn: 想象一个登录提示等着管理员放行。

abstract.en: Picture a gate opening only for the approved.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门只为获准者打开。

examples.en: The bank authorized the wire transfer.
examples.cn: 银行核准了这笔电汇。

examples.en: Only managers can authorize a discount.
examples.cn: 只有经理能批准折扣。

examples.en: He is not authorized to access the files.
examples.cn: 他未获授权访问这些文件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：author「开创者」加 -ize「使……」——让开创者的分量落到某件事上，就是批准、授权；美式拼 -ize。

root: 拉丁语 augere「使生长」派生 auctor「开创者」与 auctoritas「分量、权力」，中世纪拉丁语 auctorizare「赋予权力」经古法语 autoriser 进入英语；美式拼作 -ize，英式拼作 -ise。

sensesIntro.en: One idea, lending official weight, spreads to permitting an act, empowering a person, clearing money, granting access, sanctioning force and fixing a version.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个核心「借出正式分量」展开为准许某事、授权某人、核准钱款、给予访问、批准武力与确定版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed permission taking effect so that an act is allowed to proceed
core.cn: 核心意象：一份许可签字生效，某件事被放行

branches.en: a committee permitting a project
officers empowered to search
a card system clearing a charge
a login allowed, or force sanctioned
branches.cn: 登录被放行，或武力获批

intro.en: The verb ending -ize turns the authority stem into an action; the same stem builds the noun and the adjective.
intro.cn: 动词词尾 -ize 把「权力」词干变成动作；同一词干还造出名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin auctorizare, to give authority, comes from auctoritas and auctor, from augere, to increase.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 auctorizare「赋予权力」来自 auctoritas 与 auctor，再来自 augere「增加」。

definition_zh: 自传；自传体写作；自述生平
definition_en: the story of a person's life written by that person; the writing of such a story as a genre
core_image: 一个人既是执笔的作者，又是书里的主角
scene: 退休后，她把一生的日记整理成一本书。She published her autobiography at the age of seventy.
sceneCN: 这里 autobiography 是「自传」（第 1 个义项）；句意是她在七十岁时出版了自己的自传。

pos.zh: 名词：自传；自传体写作

derivatives.zh: 加形容词后缀：自传体的
加副词后缀：以自传方式
同族基础词：传记（他人写）

senses.title: A life story written by oneself
senses.definition: a book in which a person writes the story of his or her own life
senses.definitionCN: 一个人书写自己一生故事的书
senses.example: His autobiography covers the war years in detail.
senses.exampleCN: 他的自传详细记述了战争年代。
senses.why: The prefix auto- means self, so the writer and the subject are the same person, unlike a biography.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 auto- 意为「自己」，所以作者与主角是同一个人，这一点与传记不同。

senses.title: The genre of self-written life
senses.definition: the writing of one's own life as a literary form or practice
senses.definitionCN: 把自己一生写下来这一文学形式或写作实践
senses.example: She teaches autobiography as a literary genre.
senses.exampleCN: 她把自传作为一种文学体裁来教。
senses.why: The word can name the whole activity rather than one book, so it is often uncountable in this sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指整个写作活动而非某一本书，所以这个义项常不可数。

senses.title: A self-account within a larger work
senses.definition: a passage or section in which a person tells his or her own story
senses.definitionCN: 一个人讲述自己经历的一段文字或章节
senses.example: The opening chapter is a brief autobiography.
senses.exampleCN: 开篇第一章是一段简短的自述。
senses.why: The same self-writing can appear as a part of a bigger book, so the word shrinks to a section.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「自我书写」也可以出现在更大著作的一部分里，于是这个词缩小为一个章节。

senses.title: A life revealed through choices
senses.definition: something that reveals a person's life and character, as if it were a self-written story
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛自我书写般透露一个人生平与性情的东西
senses.example: The house is an autobiography in stone.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子就是一部石头写成的自传。
senses.why: By metaphor, anything that lays bare a life can be called an autobiography, even without words.
senses.whyCN: 通过隐喻，任何袒露一生的东西都可称为自传，哪怕没有文字。

intro.en: Autobiography joins three Greek pieces: auto-, self, bios, life, and graphia, writing, so it is self-life-writing.
intro.cn: autobiography 拼合三个希腊语成分：auto-「自己」、bios「生命」、graphia「书写」，合起来就是「自己写自己的一生」。

items.en: Autos meant self, the same element that opens automatic and autocrat.
items.cn: autos 意为「自己」，与「自动的」「独裁者」两词开头是同一成分。

items.en: Bios meant life, and gives biology and biography.
items.cn: bios 意为「生命」，产生生物学与传记。

items.en: Graphia meant writing, from graphein, to write, and gives -graphy in many fields.
items.cn: graphia 意为「书写」，来自 graphein「写」，构成许多学科词尾的「……学、……写法」。

items.en: Biography, the writing of another person's life, was established in English by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 传记，即书写他人一生，到十七世纪已在英语中确立。

items.en: The self-writing compound is recorded in the late eighteenth century, adding auto- to biography.
items.cn: 这个「自我书写」的复合词在十八世纪晚期有记录，是在传记前加上 auto-。

items.en: Today it names both a book and a genre, and it is a staple of celebrity and political publishing.
items.cn: 如今它既指一本书也指一种体裁，是名人与政治出版的常见门类。

note.en: The look-alike group is the life-writing family; the near-meaning group sorts first-person records by scope and form.
note.cn: 形近组是「写人生」词族；近义组按范围与形式区分各种第一人称记录。

entries.definition: the story of a life written by another
entries.definitionCN: 传记；由他人书写的一生，少了 auto-。

entries.definition: a person who writes their own life
entries.definitionCN: 自传作者；同族指人名词。

entries.definition: relating to a self-written life
entries.definitionCN: 自传体的；同族形容词。

entries.definition: a person's own signature
entries.definitionCN: 亲笔签名；同前缀 auto-，但写的是名字而非一生。

entries.definition: a record of part of a life, often by theme
entries.definitionCN: 回忆录；截取片段或主题，不像自传求全。

entries.definition: a daily private record of events
entries.definitionCN: 日记；逐日私密记录，未经回顾整理。

entries.definition: a personal record of thoughts and events
entries.definitionCN: 日志；个人记录，介于日记与回忆录之间。

entries.definition: an account of a life, told or written
entries.definitionCN: 生平故事；中性说法，不指明作者是谁。

normalIntro.en: Autobiography is auto- plus bio plus -graphy: self, life, writing, all in one word.
normalIntro.cn: autobiography 就是 auto- 加 bio 加 -graphy：自己、生命、书写，三块拼成一个词。

normal.en: Auto- means self, as in automatic.
normal.cn: auto- 意为「自己」，如自动的。

normal.en: Bio- means life, as in biology.
normal.cn: bio- 意为「生命」，如生物学。

normal.en: -graphy means writing, as in geography.
normal.cn: -graphy 意为「书写」，如地理学。

normal.en: A biography is written by someone else.
normal.cn: 传记由别人来写。

normal.en: A memoir covers only part of a life.
normal.cn: 回忆录只覆盖一生的一部分。

abstract.en: Picture one person holding both pen and mirror.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人同时握着笔和镜子。

abstract.en: Picture a life laid out as chapters on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一生被摊成桌上的一个个章节。

abstract.en: Picture a house that tells its owner's story.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋房子讲述主人的故事。

examples.en: She wrote her autobiography after retiring.
examples.cn: 她退休后写了自传。

examples.en: The autobiography became an instant bestseller.
examples.cn: 这本自传一出版就成了畅销书。

examples.en: He is best known for his candid autobiography.
examples.cn: 他最为人知的是那部坦率的自传。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：auto「自己」+ bio「生命」+ graphy「书写」——自己写自己的一生，就是自传；别人写你，就是传记。

root: 希腊语 autos「自己」+ bios「生命」+ graphia「书写」，先有 biography「传记」，十八世纪晚期加 auto- 构成 autobiography「自传」；同族有 autobiographer 与 autobiographical。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person who is both the writer holding the pen and the subject in the book

intro.en: Three Greek pieces build the word: auto- self, bio- life, -graphy writing; the same pieces build related words.

latinIntro.en: The elements are Greek rather than Latin; Latin biography and graphium are later borrowings of the same Greek roots.

senses.title: A ruler with absolute power
senses.definition: a ruler, such as a tsar or emperor, holding unlimited political power
senses.definitionCN: 握有无限政治权力的统治者，如沙皇、皇帝
senses.example: The Russian tsar styled himself an autocrat of all the Russias.
senses.exampleCN: 俄国沙皇自称「全俄罗斯的专制君主」。
senses.why: The Greek parts mean self and power: one person is the whole government.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语成分意为「自身」与「权力」：一人即整个政府。

senses.title: A domineering person
senses.definition: anyone who insists on deciding everything and tolerates no dissent
senses.definitionCN: 坚持独断一切、不容异议的人
senses.example: Grandfather was a benevolent autocrat at the dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 祖父在餐桌上是个仁慈的独裁者。
senses.why: The political type was so vivid that homes and kitchens inherited the word.
senses.whyCN: 政治形象过于鲜明，家庭与厨房便继承了这个词。

senses.title: Of regimes and systems
senses.definition: a ruler who embodies autocracy as a system of government
senses.definitionCN: 体现独裁政体的统治者
senses.example: Nineteenth-century Europe was a family of autocrats.
senses.exampleCN: 十九世纪的欧洲是一个独裁君主家族。
senses.why: Where autocracy is the constitution, its occupant is the autocrat.
senses.whyCN: 专制既是国体，其占据者便是 autocrat。

senses.title: The benevolent autocrat
senses.definition: an absolute ruler or boss who claims to dictate for the good of all
senses.definitionCN: 自称一切独断皆为众人福祉的绝对统治者或上司
senses.example: He ran the school as a benevolent autocrat and modernized it completely.
senses.exampleCN: 他以开明专制者的方式治校，将其彻底现代化。
senses.why: Power without consent excuses itself as wisdom; the phrase records the excuse.
senses.whyCN: 不经同意的权力常以智慧自辩；这个短语记录的正是这种辩解。

senses.title: In the workplace
senses.definition: a manager who decides without consulting the team
senses.definitionCN: 不经团队商议便自行决断的管理者
senses.example: Staff turnover revealed the new director was an autocrat.
senses.exampleCN: 员工流失率暴露出新主管是个独断专行者。
senses.why: Management language borrowed the political type to grade its bosses.
senses.whyCN: 管理学借来这个政治形象为自己的上司分等。

senses.title: In history writing
senses.definition: a historical figure characterized as concentrating power personally
senses.definitionCN: 被描述为个人集权的历史人物
senses.example: Historians debate whether the first emperor was an autocrat or a reformer.
senses.exampleCN: 史家争论开国皇帝究竟是独裁者还是改革者。
senses.why: History sorts rulers by how much they shared, and autocrat marks the bottom of the scale.
senses.whyCN: 史学按「分权多少」为君主排序，autocrat 标在这条标尺的底端。

senses.title: In family life
senses.definition: a family member who dominates household decisions
senses.definitionCN: 支配家庭决策的家庭成员
senses.example: Aunt Agatha was the acknowledged autocrat of the household.
senses.exampleCN: 阿加莎姨妈是公认的一家之主（独断者）。
senses.why: The word's bite makes it a favorite of novelists sketching tyrannical aunts and fathers.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的讥刺劲儿使它成了小说家刻画暴君式姑妈与父亲的偏爱。

senses.title: Autocrat versus related rulers
senses.titleCN: autocrat 与近义统治者之辨
senses.definition: distinguished from tyrant, despot, and dictator by its systemic, Greek-derived tone
senses.definitionCN: 与「tyrant」、「despot」、「dictator」相区别：语气更具政体性与希腊色彩
senses.example: A dictator seizes power; an autocrat inherits or claims it as a system.
senses.exampleCN: 「dictator」靠夺取上台；「autocrat」则以体制继承或自封集权。
senses.why: Each word for absolute rule carries its own biography: seizure, household, or system.
senses.whyCN: 每个「绝对统治者」的称呼都自带出身：或夺取、或家宅、或体制。

intro.en: Autocrat comes from Greek autokrates, ruling by oneself, from autos, self, plus kratos, power; Russian tsars popularized the title in the eighteenth century, and English adopted both the title and the mocking domestic use.
intro.cn: autocrat 出自希腊语 autokrates「独自统治」，由 autos「自身」加 kratos「权力」构成；18 世纪俄国沙皇的帝号使其广为人知，英语随之收入该称号及其戏谑的家用义。

items.en: Greek kratos, power or strength, is generally traced to an Indo-European root for strength; the exact reconstructed shape is disputed.
items.cn: 希腊语 kratos「权力、力量」一般被认为出自表示「强壮」的原始印欧语词根，具体重构形式尚有争议。

items.en: autos meant self and kratos meant power; autokrates meant ruling alone, autokrator the ruler who does.
items.cn: 希腊语 autos 意为「自身」，kratos 意为「权力」；autokrates 意为独自统治，autokrator 即如此行事之人。

items.en: autokrator was a Greek title for commanders and emperors with full authority.
items.cn: autokrator 是授予全权统帅与皇帝的希腊称号。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the tsars' title, translated as autocrat, made the word famous across Europe.
items.cn: 18 世纪，沙皇的头衔被译作 autocrat，使这个词风行欧洲。

items.en: English recorded autocrat in the 1760s, at first referring to the tsar and other absolute monarchs.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪 60 年代记录下 autocrat，最初指沙皇等绝对君主。

items.en: Nineteenth-century essayists extended it to any bossy person, from railway directors to aunts.
items.cn: 19 世纪随笔作家将其扩展到一切专横之人，从铁路公司董事到姑妈。

note.cn: 第一组收 kratos 词族及 auto- 形近词；第二组收相邻的绝对统治者称呼。

senses.title: Of a system with unlimited power
senses.definition: relating to a government in which one person or group holds absolute power
senses.definitionCN: 与一人或一集团掌握绝对权力的政体有关的
senses.example: The country had an autocratic constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家有一部专制的宪法。
senses.why: Auto- means self and kratos means power, so the word literally describes power held by oneself alone.
senses.whyCN: auto- 意为「自己」，kratos 意为「权力」，所以这个词字面就是「权力只归自己」。

senses.title: Of a person who decides alone
senses.definition: describing a person who makes decisions alone and tolerates no disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 形容独自作决定、不容异议的人
senses.example: Her autocratic manner annoyed the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她独断的作风惹恼了整个团队。
senses.why: The political sense transfers to daily life: a boss or parent who rules like a monarch is autocratic.
senses.whyCN: 政治义转到日常：像君主一样发号施令的上司或家长就是独断的。

senses.title: Of a manner that brooks no reply
senses.definition: showing a tone or attitude that expects obedience without question
senses.definitionCN: 表现出要求无条件服从的语气或态度
senses.example: He gave the order in an autocratic tone.
senses.exampleCN: 他用专横的语气下了命令。
senses.why: From the person the word narrows to the way they speak: a voice that leaves no room for answer.
senses.whyCN: 词义从人缩小到说话方式：一种不留回应余地的语气。

senses.title: Of power concentrated at the top
senses.definition: describing an organization where authority is concentrated in very few hands
senses.definitionCN: 形容权力集中在极少数人手里的组织
senses.example: The firm runs on autocratic lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司按高度集权的方式运作。
senses.why: The idea of one ruler scales to a structure: decisions flow from the top with no debate below.
senses.whyCN: 「一个统治者」的想法放大到结构：决定自上而下，下面没有讨论。

senses.title: Of a household run by one will
senses.definition: describing a family or small group dominated by the will of one member
senses.definitionCN: 形容由一名成员的意志主导的家庭或小团体
senses.example: It was an autocratic household where children never spoke first.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个专断的家庭，孩子从不先开口。
senses.why: The smallest stage for one-person rule is the home, so the word reaches domestic life.
senses.whyCN: 一人统治最小的舞台是家庭，于是这个词也进入家庭生活。
